(only in Il.) ; ἔντεα μαρμαίροντα Il. 12.195, cf. 16.664, al. ; τεύχεα μ. 18.617 ; Τρῶες… χαλκῷ μαρμαίροντες 13.801 ; σὺν ἔντεσι μαρμαίροντας 16.279 ; δώματα… χρύσεα μαρμαίροντα 13.22 ; ὄμματα μαρμαίροντα the sparkling eyes of Aphrodite, 3.397 ; αὐγὴ μαρμαίρουσα κεραυνοῦ Hes. Th. 699 ; μαρμαίρει δὲ δόμος χάλκῳ Alc. 15.1 ; χρυσῷ ἐλέφαντί τε μ. οἶκοι B. Fr. 16.9 ; νύκτα… ἄστροισι μαρμαίρουσαν A. Th. 401 ; χρυσῷ χαίταν μαρμαίρων, of Apollo, E. Ion 888 (lyr.) ; ἀστὴρ μαρμαίρων DP. 329 ; μαρμαίρουσι παρηΐδες AP 5.281 (Agath.), cf. Alciphr. 3.67 ; also in late Prose, Phld. Po. 2.40, Plu. Caes. 6, Luc. DMeretr. 13.3, Alciphr. l.c.
αἱ τῷ ἐρυθροδάνῳ βεβαμμέναι, Hsch.
ὁ, marble-mason, IG 4.375 (Corinth), 14.1093.
α, ον, = μαρμάρεος, Hsch.

α, ον, flashing, gleaming, esp. of metals, αἰγίς, ἄντυξ, Il. 17.594, 18.480 ; πύλαι Hes. Th. 811 ; ἅλα μαρμαρέην the twinkling sea, Il. 14.273 ; αὐγαὶ μ. Ar. Nu. 287 (lyr.) ; ἄστρα Orph. Fr. 168.13.
of marble, λίθος IG 7.2544 (Thebes) ; στήλη ib. 14.1603 ; δόμος AP 6.123 (Anyt.), cf. PRyl. 227.16 (iii AD).
work in marble, Tz. H. 9.127.
= μαρμαίρω, ἀκτῖνας προσώπου μαρμαριζούσας Pi. Fr. 123.2 ; ἡ μαρμαρίζουσα πέτρα, of quartz rock containing gold, DS. 3.12.
ή, όν, either prepared from marble or obtained from Marmarica (Barca), ἄσβεστος PHolm. 25.19.
η, ον, of marble, ἄγαλμα Theoc. Ep. 10.2 ; τάφος AP 7.649 (Anyt.) ; τροχοί DS. 17.45 ; εἰκών, ἄγαλμα, GDI 3502 (Cnidus), SIG 996.14 (Smyrna) ; λίθος J. AJ 7.10.3.
ιδος, ἡ, like marble, πέτρα Ph.Byz. Mir. 2.3. = ἀγλαοφῶτις, Plin. HN 24.160.
ου, ὁ, = marmorum sculptor, Gloss.
ἡ, sculpture in marble, Str. 10.5.7.
εσσα, εν, = μαρμάρεος, Ὀλύμπου μ. αἴγλαν S. Ant. 610 (lyr.).
ἡ, stucco made from marble, Sch. Hes. Sc. 142.

τό, marble, Call. Ap. 24, SIG 909.5 (v AD).
sore on the feet of asses, Hippiatr. 53.
όν, working in marble, Gloss.
ον, with gleaming wings, κόλποι Ἀμφιτρίτας Tim. Pers. 39 (prob.).
Μαρός, ὁ, pl. Μᾶρες, a tribe near Colchis, Hes. (?) ap. Sch. Il. Oxy. 221 iii 3, Hecat. 205 J., Hdt. 3.94, 7.79, UPZ 149.4 (iii BC).

ὁ, a crystalline rock, which sparkles (< μαρμαίρει) in the light, μάρμαρος ὀκριόεις Il. 12.380, Od. 9.499, cf. E. Ph. 663 (lyr.), Ar. Ach. 1172 (lyr.) ; as Adj., πέτρος μ. ὀκριόεις Il. 16.735, cf. E. Ph. 1401, etc. later, marble, μάρμαρον ἢ λίθον λευκήν Hp. Mul. 2.185, cf. Thphr. Lap. 9 ; also fem., μαρμάρου… τῆς Πεντελικῆς μέταλλα Str. 9.1.23 ; μ. λίθος Id. 14.1.35 ; hence, work in marble, i.e. tombstone, τυκτὴ μ. Theoc. 22.211.
chips made by cutting marble (masc.), Plu. 2.660c, 954a, Dsc. 5.79.
ὁ, marble-mason, Tz. H. 9.131.
ές, gleaming white, στόματος παῖδες, of the teeth, Tim. Pers. 103.

coat with marble stucco, [κίονας] Jul. Ep. 80 ; — Pass., PMagBerol. 1.109.
line with marble, κολυμβήθρα… μεμαρμαρώσθω Hero Stereom. 2.5. Pass., to be turned to stone, Lyc. 826.
στερεόν, Hsch.

ἡ, 1.
flashing, sparkling, gleaming, λάμπει δ’ ὑπὸ μαρμαρυγαῖς ὁ χρυσός B. 3.17, cf. Pl. Criti. 116c, Plu. Caes. 69 ; ἡ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ μ. Dam. Pr. 213 ; αἱ ἀπολάμπουσαι ἀπὸ τῶν ὀμμάτων μ. Damian. Opt. 2, cf. Adam. 1.16.
2. ΄seeing sparks΄, Hp. Prog. 24 (pl.), Pl. R. 518a. of any quick motion, μαρμαρυγαὶ ποδῶν the quick twinkling of the dancers’ feet. Od. 8.265, cf. h.Ap. 203.
ατος, τό, = μαρμαρυγή 2, Cael.Aur. TP 1.62 (pl.).
ες, ΄seeing sparks΄, ὄμματα Hp. Acut. 42 ; μαρμαρυγῶδές τι πρὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν Id. Prorrh. 2.35.
ἀπὸ τοῦ μαρμαίρειν, Hsch.
flash, sparkle, Them. Or. 20.235b ; of the eyes, Adam. 1.16, al. ; of stars, twinkle, Jul. Gal. 356e.
ες, like marble, Et.Gud. 499.21.
ιδος, ἡ, turning to stone by a glance, Lyc. 843 ; as riddling synonym for Ἀθηναία, Trypho Trop. p. 195 S.
όν, with sparkling eyes, Λύσσα E. HF 884 (lyr.).
εως, ἡ, production of μάρμαρον II, Hippiatr. 100.
ή, όν, afflicted with μάρμαρον II, Hippiatr. 53.

μάρνασαι Pi. N. 10.86, μάρναται Il. 4.513, μάρνανται E. Med. 249 ; imper. μάρναο Il. 15.475 ; subj. μαρνώμεσθα Hes. Sc. 110 ; opt. μαρναίμεθα Od. 11.513 ; inf. μάρνασθαι Il. 5.33, E. Tr. 731 ; part. μαρνάμενος Il. 3.307, Tyrt. 12.33, E. Ph. 1574 (lyr.) ; impf. ἐμαρνάμην Anacreont. 12.11 ; -αο, ατο, Od. 22.228, Il. 12.40 (Ep. μάρνατο 11.498) ; 3 dual ἐμαρνάσθην 7.301 ; pl. ἐμαρνάμεσθα E. Ph. 1142, IT 1376 ; poet. μαρνάμεθα Od. 3.108, B. 5.125, μάρναντο Il. 13.169 ; only pres. and impf. :
fight, do battle, τινι with, against another, Il. 15.475, etc. ; ἐπί τινι 9.317 ; πρός τινα E. Tr. 731 ; σύν τινι together with another, on his side, Od. 3.85 ; ἀμφί τινα about a fallen hero, Il. 16.775 ; περί τινος for or about a person, ib. 497 ; ἐναντίοι ἀλλήλοισι νίκης καὶ κράτεος πέρι μ. Hes. Th. 647 ; γῆς πέρι καὶ παίδων Tyrt. l.c. ; περὶ δορᾶς Κουρῆσι B. l.c. ; μήλων ἕνεκ’ Hes. Op. 163 ; c. dat. instrum., ἔγχεϊ, χαλκῷ μ., Il. 16.195, 497 ; φασγάνῳ, δορί, Pi. P. 9.21, E. Med. l.c. of boxers, Od. 18.31.
quarrel, wrangle, Il. 1.257.
contend, strive, Pi. P. 2.65 ; ἀμφ’ ἀρεταῖσι, ἐσλοῖσι πέρι, Id. O. 5.15, N. 5.47 ; κασιγνήτου πέρι ib. 10.86 ; μ. φυᾷ strive with all one΄s natural powers, ib. 1.25. — Ep. and Lyr. Verb, used also by E. ; cf. βάρναμαι. (Cf. Skt. mṛṇā´ti ΄crush΄.)
ὁ, name of Zeus at Gaza, St.Byz. s.v. Γάζα, LW 2412g (Haurân), Marin. Procl. 19 ; Μαρνεῖον, τό, his temple, Marc.Diac. Vit. Porph. 64.
τό, a kind of sage, Teucrium Marum, Mnesim. 4.61 (anap.), Thphr. Od. 33, Dsc. 3.42.
τό, = θριδακίνη, lettuce, Gp. 12.1.2, Alex.Trall. 2, Verm. p. 593 P. ; cf. μαιούλιον.
ὁ, seizer, ravisher, A. Supp. 826 (lyr.) ; μάρπτυς (sic) ; ὑβριστής, Hsch.

impf. ἔμαρπτον Il. 21.489 ; Ep. μάρπτον Emp. 90.1 ; fut. μάρψω Il. 15.137, E. Ion 158 (lyr.) ; aor.1 ἔμαρψα Il. 22.201, etc. ; Ep. forms, 3 sg. subj. μάρπτῃσι Il. 8.405 ; aor.2 opt. μεμάποιεν Hes. Sc. 252 ; inf. μαπέειν ib. 231, 304 ; 3 sg. pf. μέμαρπεν ib. 245 ; part. μεμαρπώς Id. Op. 204, ARh. 1.756 ; — Pass., μαρπτομένη Call. Dian. 195 ; — poet. (chiefly Ep.) Verb, take hold of, τινα Il. 14.346, etc. ; c. gen. partis, catch by…, αὐχένων χερσὶν ὄφιας Pi. N. 1.45 ; μάρψας ποδός νιν S. Tr. 779 ; c. dat. instrum., χεῖρας ἔμαρπτε σκαιῇ Il. 21.489 ; φάρμακα χερσίν Emp. 23.3 ; χερσὶν ἡνίας E. Hipp. 1188 ; γαμφηλῇσι δράκοντα Orac. ap. Ar. Eq. 197 ; χερὶ ἀνθέματος AP 6.199 (Antiphil.). — Special usages ; in a hostile sense, lay hold of, seize, αὐτίχ’ ἕνα μάρψας ἑτάρων Od. 10.116 ; of sleep, τὸν ὕπνος ἔμαρπτε Il. 23.62 ; γῆράς τε μέμαρπεν Hes. Sc. 245, cf. καταμάρπτω overtake, catch a fugitive, μή με μεταΐξας μάρψῃ ταχέεσσι πόδεσσι Il. 21.564, cf. 22.201, Archil. 59 ; but χθόνα μάρπτε ποδοῖϊν took hold of ground with her feet, Il. 14.228 ; ἕλκεα…, ἅ κεν μάρπτῃσι κεραυνός which the thunderbolt shall inflict (by laying hold), 8.405, 419 ; μ. σθένος gain strength, of a fallow field, Pi. N. 6.11 ; εἴ σε μάρψει ψῆφος if the votes shall condemn, A. Eu. 597 ; ἄσκοποι πλάκες ἔμαρψαν the unseen land engulfed him, S. OC 1681 (lyr.) ; τόξοις μ. τινά E. Ion 158 (lyr.) ; τὰ ὄλβια τῦφος ἔμαρψεν CratesTheb 8 ; of death, μάρψεν ᾍδης Trag.Adesp. 208 ; esp. in epitaphs, μάρψασα μοῖρα IG 4.620 (Argos), 7.115 (Megara), cf. 12(7).115 (Amorgos). (From μṛπτω, cf. βράπτω.)
τό, iron spade, Hsch. (Semitic or Sumerian word, cf. Assyr. marru ΄hoe΄, ΄pick΄.)
= μαρσίππιον.
τό, Dim. of μάρσιππος.

ὁ, bag, pouch, X. An. 4.3.11, PPetr. 3 p. 257 (iii BC), PSI 4.427.1, al. (iii BC), PCair. Zen. 69.14 (iii BC), LXX Ge. 42.27, al., f.l. in DS. 20.41 ; poultice, Sor. 2.10, 59 ; μ. λινοῦς, = κρησέρα, Gal. 19.115 ; — Dim. μαρσίππιον, τό, Hp. Acut. 21, Apollod. Car. 13, PCair. Zen. 10.27, al. (iii BC), PPetr. 3 p. 145 (iii BC), LXX Pr. 1.14. [μάρσιππος, μαρσίππιον, Pap. ll. cc. and usu. in LXX ; μάρσιπος, μαρσίπιον freq.v.l. in later codd., cf. Gloss. ; μαρσείπειον UPZ 77ii 13 (ii BC, illiterate) ; μάρσυπος, μαρσύπιον, Gloss. ; μαρσυπεῖον v.l. in LXX Si. 18.33 ; μάρσυππος, μαρσύππιον, Hsch. s. vv. ἀρυβαλίδα, ἀρύβαλλοι.]
= μαρσύπιον.
τό, Dim. of μάρσυπος.
v. μάρσιππος.
τό, Dim. of μάρσυππος.
v. μάρσιππος.
ὁ (sc. μήν), Lat. Martius, the month of March, Plu. Num. 19, DC. 71.33.

ὁ, man-eater, i.e. tiger, described with fabulous attributes by Ctes. ap. Arist. HA 501a26 (v.l. μαρτιοχώρας, μαντιχώρας), cf. Ctes. Fr. 57.7, Id. ap. Paus. 9.21.4 (μαρτιόρα codd.), et ap. Ael. NA 4.21. (Cf. Opers. martiya- ΄man΄, Avest. khwar- ΄eat΄, Mod.Pers. mard-khwār ΄man-eater΄.)

fut. -ήσω Pi. O. 6.21 ; — Pass., fut. μαρτυρηθήσομαι Is. 8.13, D. 19.40 ; μαρτυρήσομαι in pass. sense, X. (v. infr. 9), D. 57.37 ; aor. ἐμαρτυρήθην ; pf. μεμαρτύρημαι Antipho 6.16, used in act. sense, LXX Ge. 43.3 : — bear witness, give evidence ; — Constr. ; abs., Simon. 4.7, Pi. I. 5 (4).48 ; μαρτυροῦντι πιστεύειν Antipho 2.2.7 ; ἐξέστω καὶ τοῖς δούλοις μαρτυρεῖν PLille 29.20 (iii BC), cf. SIG 953.19 (Calymna, ii BC), etc. c. dat. pers., bear witness to or in favour of another, confirm what he says, A. Eu. 594, Hdt. 8.94, etc. ; μαρτυρέει μοι τῇ γνώμῃ, ὅτι… bears witness to my opinion, that…, Id. 2.18, cf. 4.29 ; μαρτυρεῖς σαυτῷ E. Ion 532 ; esp. bear favourable witness to, give a good report of a person, IG2². 657 (iii BC), etc. ; πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ Eu. Luc. 4.22. BC dat. rei, μ. τῇ διαθήκῃ POxy. 494.33 (ii AD), etc. c. acc. rei, testify to a thing, Alc. 102, Pi. O. 13.108, S. Ant. 515, Pl. Phdr. 244d ; μ. τινί τι Pi. O. 6.21, A. Supp. 797 (lyr.). μ. περί τινος Pl. Ap. 21a ; ὑπέρ τινος D. 29.54. c. inf., testify that a thing is, Heraclit. 34, S. OC 1265, etc. ; τίς σοι μαρτυρήσει ταῦτ’ ἐμοῦ κλύειν ; that he heard… ? Id. Tr. 422, cf. E. Hipp. 977 ; ὁ κληθεὶς μαρτυρείτω ἀληθῆ μαρτυρεῖν PHal. 1.225 (iii BC) ; rarely c. part., μαρτυρεῖτέ [μοι]… ῥινηλατούσῃ A. Ag. 1184 ; μ. τισὶ παραγινομέναις DH. 8.46. μ. τινὶ ὡς… A. Ag. 494, cf. Pl. Grg. 523c ; σώματα… ὡς ἔστιν, αὐτὴ ἡ αἴσθησις… μ. Epicur. Ep. 1 p. 6U. ; μ. ὅτι… X. Vect. 4.25. μ. τινὶ τῆς συμμαχίας testify to, acknowledge the value of his alliance, J. AJ 13.5.3. c. acc. cogn., μαρτυρίαν μ. Is. 11.25, Pl. Erx. 399b ; μ. ἀκοήν give hearsay evidence, D. 57.4 ; μ. ψεῦδος, ψεύδη, bear false witness, Amips. 13, Diph. 32.16 ; τὰ ψευδῆ Lys. 19.4 ; τἀληθῆ Aeschin. 1.46 ; — Pass., μαρτυρίαι μαρτυρηθεῖσαι D. 47.1 ; μεμαρτύρηταί τι περί τινος Antipho 6.16, cf. Lys. 13.66. impers. in Pass., παρ’ ἄλλου ποιητοῦ μαρτυρεῖται testimony is borne by…, Pl. Prt. 344d ; οἶδα… μαρτυρήσεσθαί μοι ὅτι… X. Mem. 4.8.10, cf. Ap. 26 ; μεμαρτύρηται ὑμῖν testimony has been given before you, Lys. 19.55, Is. 9.5. Pass., μαρτυρεῖταί μοι σοφία is ascribed to me, DH. 2.26 ; μαρτυροῦμαι ἐμπειρίαν I have it ascribed to me, Plu. 2.58a, cf. Luc. Sacr. 10 ; καλοκἀγαθίαν μαρτυρούμενος J. AJ 15.10.5 ; μαρτυροῦμαι ἐπί τινι I bear a character for…, Ath. 1.25 f ; ἄνδρας μαρτυρουμένους men whose character is approved by testimony, Act. Ap. 6.3 ; τεχνίτας… μαρτυρηθέντας ὑπό τινος SIG 799.28 (Cyzicus, i AD) ; δι’ ὅλης οἰκουμένης μαρτυρούμενον θεόν Sammelb. 1070 (Abydos).
Astrol., to be in aspect with, c. dat., Ptol. Tetr. 123 ; μ. τὴν μοῖραν Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.226 ; — Pass., Nech. ap. Vett.Val. 279.23.
ατος, τό, testimony, E. Supp. 1204.
εως, ἡ, corroborative evidence, ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν φαινομένων μ. Sor. 1.41.
one must testify, Dsc. Praef. 2.
ή, όν, complimentary, ψηφίσματα μ. καὶ τιμητικά Jahresh. 13.201 (Alabanda, ii AD).

ἡ, testimony, Διονύσου μαρτυρίῃσι Od. 11.325, cf. Hes. Op. 282 (pl.) ; freq. both sg. and pl., μ. τινός his evidence, Antipho 2.2.7 ; μ. παρέχεσθαι Pl. Smp. 179b ; εἰς μ. κληθῆναι Id. Lg. 937a ; μαρτυριῶν ἀπέχεσθαι to refuse to give evidence, Ar. Eq. 1316 ; ἐμβάλλεσθαι μ. ψευδῆ D. 54.31 ; γράφειν μ. τινί serve him with a subpoena, Aeschin. 1.45 ; μ. ἔχειν παρά τινων ἔκ τινων Arist. Pol. 1338a36 ; in non-legal sense, commendation, πάσης μ. ἐπιτήδειον (in sense of ἄξιον) SIG 1073.17 (Olympia, ii AD) ; in pl., demonstrations of favour, POxy. 41.18 (iii/iv AD).
Astrol., aspect, Vett.Val. 5.5, Gal. 19.532, Man. 1.124, Procl. Par. Ptol. 255.

τό, testimony, proof, πρῶτον καὶ μέγιστον μ. Hdt. 2.22, cf. Pi. I. 4 (3).10, etc. ; freq. in pl., μαρτύρια θέσθαι Hdt. 8.55, cf. A. Ag. 1095 (lyr.), Eu. 485, 797 ; μετ’ ἀειμνήστου μ. Th. 1.33 ; μαρτύριον δέ…, folld. by γάρ, here is a proof, namely…, ib. 8, etc. ; μέγα τόδε μ.,… γάρ Hdt. 8.120. τὰ μ. the tables of the Decalogue, LXX Le. 16.13, al.
shrine of a martyr, Aët. 15.15 (a) Z., POxy. 941.4 (vi AD), etc.
τό, written deposition, Anon. in Rh. 159.8.

fut. μαρτυροῦμαι (δια-) LXX Ps. 80 (81).9 (cod. Alex.) ; aor. ἐμαρτυράμην Pl. Phlb. 47d, App. BC 2.47 : — call to witness, invoke, c. acc. pers., Antipho 1.29, S. OC 813, etc. ; esp. of the gods, Ἄρτεμιν, γαῖαν καὶ θεούς, E. Hipp. 1451, Ph. 626 ; δαίμονας, ὡς… Id. Med. 619 ; c. acc. et inf., ὑμᾶς δ’ ἀκούειν ταῦτ’ ἐγὼ μαρτύρομαι A. Eu. 643, etc. ; c. part., μαρτύρομαι τυπτόμενος I call you to witness that…, Ar. Av. 1031, cf. E. HF 858 (troch.). c. acc. rei, call one to witness a thing, Hdt. 1.44, Ar. Ra. 528, Pl. 932.
protest, asseverate, μ. ὅτι… Id. Nu. 1222, Th. 6.80 ; ταῦτα Pl. l.c. ; abs., μαρτύρομαι I protest, Ar. Ach. 926, Lys. 3.15. c. acc. pers. et gen. rei, οἱ δὲ τῆς τῶν θεῶν… παραγωγῆς τὸν Ὅμηρον μ. ὅτι… cite Homer as a witness of…, Pl. R. 364d ; ἐμαυτὸν μ. τῆς φιλοτιμίας App. l.c. ; μ. τινὶ ὅτι… Ep. Gal. 5.3 ; τοὺς ἀποστάντας μ. τῆς ἐπιορκίας remind them of…, App. BC 5.129.

produce evidence, PLips. 40 iii 14 (iv/v AD), Gloss. ; — also in Med., call to witness, Corn. ND 16. mostly in Med., testify, certify on oath, IG 9(1).61.8 (Daulis, ii AD), Mitteis Chr. 242.3 (ii AD), Sammelb. 5217.20 (ii AD), etc.
ατος, τό, statement on oath, affidavit, POxy. 1114.23 (iii AD), BGU 1093.22 (iii AD), Gloss.
εως, ἡ, affirmation on oath, Sammelb. 5217.18 (ii AD). = contestatio, Gloss.
ἡ, Astrol., = μαρτυρία II, Ptol. Tetr. 183 (pl.). = testificatio, Gloss.

ὁ, Ep. form for μάρτυς, ἐστὲ μάρτυροι Il. 2.302, etc. ; also in Central Greece, IG 9(1).226 (Drymaea), 364 (Naupactus), GDI 1684, al. (Delph.), etc. ; sg. once in Od., οἷσιν ἄρα Ζεὺς μάρτυρος 16.423, cf. PGen. 54.6 (iv AD). (Zenod. rejected this form, but it is defended in Sch. Il. Oxy. 1087.22.)
υρος, ὁ and ἡ, Aeol. for Att. μάρτυς, Hdn. Gr. 1.47, al. ; also Dor., SIG 953.22 (Calymna, ii BC) ; cf. μάρτυρος, ἐπιμάρτυρος.

[ῠ] ὁ, ἡ, Cret., Epid. μαῖτυς Leg. Gort. 1.13, al., IG4²(1).42, Cret. also μαίτυρς GDI 4998 v ii ; gen. μάρτυρος, acc. -υρα Hes. Op. 371, etc., formed from μάρτυρ, exc. acc. μάρτυν Simon. 84.4, Men. 1034, Plu. 2.49a ; dat. pl. μάρτυσι (but μάρτυρσι prob. in Hippon. 51) : — witness (not in Hom.), Hes. l.c., h.Merc. 372, Thgn. 1226, etc. ; ἄμμιν μάρτυς ἔστω Ζεύς Pi. P. 4.167, cf. A. Eu. 664 ; ἁμέραι δ’ ἐπίλοιποι μ. σοφώτατοι Pi. O. 1.34 ; τούτων μάρτυρας καλῶ θεούς S. Tr. 1248, cf. E. Ph. 491 ; μάρτυρα θέσθαι τινά Id. Supp. 261 ; μ. θεοὺς ποιεῖσθαι Th. 4.87, etc. ; μάρτυρι χρῆσθαί τινι Arist. Rh. 1375b30 ; μάρτυρας παρέχεσθαι produce witnesses, Pl. Grg. 471e, cf. D. 27.51, etc. ; μάρτυρες παρίστανται X. Cyr. 1.6.16 ; μάρτυρα παράγεσθαι, μάρτυρας ἐπάγεσθαι, Pl. Lg. 836c, R. 364c ; δικάζει ταῦτα μαρτύρων ὅπο A. Supp. 934 ; μαρτύρων ἐναντίον Antipho 1.28, Ar. Ec. 448 ; ἐν μάρτυσι Pl. Smp. 175e ; τί δεῖται μάρτυρος ; Id. R. 340a.
martyr, Apoc. 2.13, etc.
Astrol., in aspect, μάρτυρες ἀλλήλων Man. 4.451. (Cf. μάρτυρ, μάρτυρος.)
Dor. for μηρυκάομαι.
Dor. for μηρυκισμός.
Dor. for μηρύομαι.
centauria, Gloss.
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, = λευκόψαρος, ὄνοι Hippiatr. 14.
ωνος, ὁ, name of Thracian priest who gave wine to Odysseus, Od. 9.197 ; hence, of a strong wine, Cratin. 135, E. Cyc. 412 ; perh. also a throw of the dice, cf. Herod. 3.25.

aor.1 ἐμασησάμην Hp. Epid. 7.11, Hsch. s.v. ἐμάσταζεν : — chew, ἀμυγδάλας μασᾶσθαι Eup. 253 ; κρέας Ar. Pl. 321 ; σηπίας Id. Ec. 554 ; τι Hp. l.c. ; πάπυρον Thphr. HP 4.8.4 ; τὰ δέρματα τῶν θυρεῶν J. BJ 6.3.3 ; abs., Ar. Eq. 717, V. 780, Thphr. Char. 20.5 ; μασώμενον, τό, of a toothache remedy, Cass.Fel. 32. — Not in Trag., or Att. Prose.
shoot out the lip, as a mark of contempt, Philostr. VA 7.21.
v. ἐπιμαίομαι.
Dor. for μᾶζα.
ὁ, = Avest. mazdayasna, "worshipper of Mazda", title of kings of the Sassanid dynasty, OGI 432.1 (Naksh-i-Rustam).
Dor. for μαζός.
[ᾰ], ατος, τό, something to chew, quid, Antiph. 244, Thphr. HP 4.8.4.
εως, ἡ, chewing, Thphr. CP 6.9.3, Ruf. Anat. 19, Gal. 6.626.
τά, food which has to be chewed, Sor. 1.115.
ῆρος, ὁ, chewer, μῦς μ. a muscle of the lower jaw, used in chewing, Hp. Art. 30, Gal. UP 16.6, Simp. in Cael. 664.4.
ατος, τό, leather, Ctes. Fr. 57.23 (pl.).

ητος, ὁ, = ἱμάσθλη, leather, Hp. Morb. 2.59 ; Aeol. μάσλης, perh. leather shoe, Sappho 19 ; thong of a whip, φοίνιον μάσθλητα δίγονον S. Fr. 129 ; μάσθλη is dub., cf. ib. 571, Hsch.
metaph, supple, slippery knave, Ar. Eq. 269, Nu. 449 (anap.), Aristid. Or. 34 (50).61.
η, ον, like leather or red as leather, καρὶς μασθλητίνη Cratin. 283, Eup. 107.
ὁ, v. μαστός.
τό, or μασθωτός, ὁ, = μαστάριον II, Zos.Alch. pp. 199, 251 B.
ον, = ἐρίγδουπος, Hsch.
gloss on νάρφη, Hsch.
intens. Prefix (like ἐρι-) ; cf. μαί.
ου, ὁ, laver, Keil-Premerstein Dritter Bericht No.42 (Jewish, iii AD). (Cf. Talmudic maskel, maskol ΄basin΄.)
δίκελλα, Hsch.
Aeol. for μάσθλης.
ατος, τό, (< μαίομαι) search, Cratin. 424 ; = ζήτημα, Pl. Cra. 421 b.
τό, = μασουχᾶς, Aët. 13.118, Paul.Aeg. 7.23.
ᾶ, ὁ, a compound remedy, Alex.Trall. 7.1, Paul.Aeg. 3.37, 7.23.

τό, the leaf of σίλφιον, Antiph. 88.4 (cj.), Thphr. HP 6.3.1.
the stalk of σίλφιον, Dsc. 3.80. = semen ferulae, Gloss.
said to be Aeol. for δῆσαι, Timae. 39.
ζητῆσαι, καθαρίσαι, φυράσαι, Hsch. (μᾶσσαι cod.).

ἡ, Marseilles, Th. 1.13, Arist. Pol. 1321a30, etc. ; — hence Μασσαλιῶται or Μασσαλιῆται, οἱ, D. 32.8, DS. 14.93, etc. ; — Adj. Μασσαλιωτικός, ή, όν, Hp. Mul. 1.78 ; — also Μασσαλιήτης οἶνος Ath. 1.27c.
v. sub Μασσαλία.
v. sub Μασσαλία.
v. sub Μασσαλία.
incorrectly written for μασάομαι.
v. μαίομαι.
incorrectly written for μάσημα.
incorrectly written for μάσησις.
incorrectly written for μασητήρ.
πορρώτερον, Hsch. ; ὡς ἔνι μ. Dius ap. Stob. 4.21.16 (nisi leg. -ότατον) ; cf. μάσσων.

S. Fr. 563 ; Att. μάττω Eup. 340 ; fut. μάξω Ar. Lys. 601 (anap.) (ἀνα- Od. 19.92) ; aor. ἔμαξα Pherecr. 183.2, Pl. R. 372b, Arist. Rh. 1416b31, Nic. Th. 952 ; pf. μέμαχα Ar. Eq. 55 ; — Med., fut. μάξομαι (ἐμμ-) Call. Dian. 124 ; aor. ἐμαξάμην Hdt. 1.200 ; poet. μαξάμην AP 5.295 (Agath.) ; — Pass., aor.1 ἐμάχθην Aret. CD 2.12 ; aor.2 ἐμάγην [α] (v. ἐκμ-) ; pf. μέμαγμαι Ar. Eq. 57, Th. 4.16 ; freq. in compds. with ἀπό, ἐκ :
knead, press into a mould, esp. of barley-cakes which were subsequently moistened and eaten without baking (cf. μακτός), S. l.c., Ar. Pax 14 ; μᾶζαν μεμαχότος Id. Eq. 55 (also in Med., Hdt. l.c., Ar. Nu. 788) ; ἐκ μὲν τῶν κριθῶν ἄλφιτα…, ἐκ δὲ τῶν πυρῶν ἄλευρα, τὰ μὲν πέψαντες, τὰ δὲ (viz. ἄλφιτα) μάξαντες Pl. l.c. ; metaph, μάττειν ἐπινοίας Ar. Eq. 539 ; — Med., εὐλόγου<ς> αἰτίας ματτόμενον Pall. in Hp. Fract. 12.286 C. ; — Pass., μᾶζα μεμαγμένη Archil. 2 ; μᾶζαν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ μεμ. Ar. Eq. 57, cf. 1167 ; σῖτος μεμαγμένος dough ready kneaded (or pressed into cakes), Th. l.c., cf. Ar. Pax 28 ; ὅστις ἀλφιτοσιτεῖ, ὕδατι μεμαγμένην (μεμιγ- codd.) ἀεὶ τὴν μᾶζαν ἐσθίει prob. cj. in X. Cyr. 6.2.28, cf. Agathocl. 6.
wipe, ῥοδόπηχυς Ἠὼς μαξαμέ[νη χεῖρας ?] Inscr.Prien. 287 ; cf. εἰσμάσσομαι.
take the impression of, cling close to, Med. c. acc., AP l.c.

ὁ and ἡ, neut. μάσσον (v. Hdn. Gr. 2.942), gen. μάσσονος, poet. Comp. of μακρός (from *μακ-yων), longer, ἔτι μ. Od. 8.203 ; μάσσον’ ἢ ὡς ἰδέμεν greater than one else could see, Pi. O. 13.113 ; μάσσον’ ἀριθμοῦ too many for counting, Id. N. 2.23 ; τὰ μάσσω μὲν τί δεῖ λέγειν ; A. Ag. 598, cf. Pers. 440 ; ὁ μ. βίοτος ib. 708 (troch.) ; [ἔλαφοι] μάσσονες ἢ ταῦροι Call. Dian. 102 ; c. acc. cogn., μῆκος μάσσων Nic. Th. 224 ; in Prose, μ. ὁδός X. Cyr. 2.4.27 ; μάσσω δρόμον (prob.) Id. Lac. 12.5. Adv., μάσσον ὡς ἐμοὶ γλυκύ (nisi leg. μάσσον’ ὧν) A. Pr. 629.
= μασάομαι, chew, eat, Nic. Th. 918.
ἡγεμών, ἢ μεγάλως, Hsch.
χάρακες, κάμακες, Hsch.

ακος, ἡ (Lyc. 687), (< μασάομαι) that with which one chews, mouth, jaws, ἐπὶ μάστακα χερσὶ πίεζε he stopped his mouth with his hands, Od. 4.287 ; με… ἑλὼν ἐπὶ μάστακα χερσίν seizing me by the mouth, 23.76, cf. Alcm. 144 ; ἀμαυρᾶς μάστακος προσφθέγμασι Lyc. l.c. ; μάστακι ποππύζων AP 5.284.6 (Agath.), cf. 293.16 (Id.). v. μύσταξ. = μάσημα, mouthful, morsel, ὡς δ’ ὄρνις ἀπτῆσι νεοσσοῖσι προφέρῃσι μάστακ΄, ἐπεί κε λάβῃσι Il. 9.324, cf. Eust. 753.62 ; μάστακα δοῖσα τέκνοισιν Theoc. 14.39 ; of the olive, Call. Iamb. 1.271 ; others expl. in Il. l.c. as dat. μάστακι in its beak, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. μάσταξ, Plu. 2.494d.
locust, S. Fr. 716, Nic. Th. 802, Clitarch. Gloss. ap. EM 216.9. (Cf. μέστακα.)

τό, Dim. of μαστός I. 2, Alciphr. 1.31 (pl.). Dim. of μαστός II. 3, prob. in IG 11(4).1307.23, 1308.2 (v. Supp.Epigr. 3.665) (Delos).
cover of an alembic, Syn.Alch. p. 60 B.
mumble, like one with his mouth full, of an old man, Ar. Ach. 689 ; cf. μασταρίζειν· μαστιχᾶσθαι, καὶ τρέμειν, κτλ., Hsch. ; — also μαστηρύζειν· τὸ κακῶς μασᾶσθαι (Cyren.), Phot.
ἡ, inquiry, μ. τεχνική Olymp. in Alc. p. 192 C.
ἡ, fem. of μαστήρ, metaph, μῆνις μ. demanding vengeance, A. Supp. 163 (lyr.) ; glossed μαστιγωτική in Sch. l.c., whence μαστίκτειρα has been conjectured in A. l.c.
= μαστεύω, GDI 1570 (Dodona, dub.).
εως, ἡ, search, IG4²(1).123.133 (Epid., iv BC) ; investigation, τινων Archim. Spir. Praef. ; search for…, c. gen., γῆς ἀμείνονος DH. 1.56.
one must inquire, Max.Tyr. 34.4.
οῦ, ὁ, = μαστήρ, X. Oec. 8.13.

Ep. impf. -εύεσκον ARh. 4.1394 ; poet. inf. μαστευέμεν Pi. P. 3.59 ; poet. aor. μάστευσα ib. 4.35 : — seek, search after, c. acc. pers. vel rei, τὴν μαστεύων Hes. Fr. 79.4 ; μαστεύων σε κιγλάνω μόλις E. Hel. 597 ; ἄλλον ἄλλη μ. [Epich.] 298, cf. IG4²(1).122.22 (Epid.) ; [χώραν] X. An. 5.6.25 ; τὰ φεύγοντα διώκειν καὶ μ. ib. 7.3.11 ; crave, need, τὰ ἐοικότα πὰρ δαιμόνων μ. Pi. P. 3.59 ; προφήτας δ’ οὔτινας μαστεύομεν A. Ag. 1099. c. inf., seek, strive to do, Pi. P. 4.35, N. 8.43, X. An. 3.1.43, Cyr. 2.2.22 ; τὸν… παῖδα μ. μαθεῖν, εἰ μηκέτ’ εἴη E. Ph. 36 ; — Med., Aesar. ap. Stob. 1.49.27, Philostr. Jun. Im. 17 ; — Pass., ἁδονὰ σφοδρότερον μαστευομένα Metop. ap. Stob. 3.1.115. — Poet. word (Hom. uses only ματεύω), also used by X., and in late Prose, Nic.Dam. 4 J., etc.

ῆρος, ὁ, (< μαίομαι) seeker, searcher, τινος S. OC 456, Tr. 733, E. Ba. 986 (lyr.) ; also in late Prose, Parth. 1.1, Alciphr. 1.11 ; μ. ἀναγκαίας ζωῆς Porph. Abst. 2.5 ; as fem., Carc. 5.5 (s.v.l.) ; cf. μάστειρα.
μαστῆρες, οἱ, officers appointed to ascertain and get possession of the assets of public debtors and exiles at Athens, Hyp. Fr. 133 ; at Amorgos, IG 12(7).62.54.
α, ον, good at search, Ἑρμῆς A. Supp. 920.
τὸ κακῶς μασᾶσθαι (Cyren.), Phot.
= μαστίζω, only in Ep. part. μαστιόων, Hes. Sc. 431.
f.l. for μαστιγόω.

= flagrum, Gloss. (dub.).
a kind of plant used in magic, PMagPar. 1.3009.
ου, ὁ, (< μάστιξ) one that wants whipping, a rogue, S. Fr. 329 (pl.), Ar. Eq. 1228, Ra. 501, Pl. Grg. 524c, Men. Pk. 134, Plu. 2.829b, etc.
Com. Desiderat. of μαστίζω, long for, i.e. deserve, a whipping, Eup. 429.
ου, τό, Dim. of μάστιξ, whip, M.Ant 10.38.
Pass., to be governed by the scourge (i.e. as slaves), DS. 8 Fr. 24.
ον, = μαστιγοφόρος, Plu. 2.553a.
bear the scourge, DS. 8 Fr. 24, Mon.Ant. 23.68 (Perga).

ον, scourge-bearing, ὑπηρέται Arist. Ath. 35.1 ; epith. of Ajax, Arg. S. Aj. Subst., policeman, esp. at the Games, Th. 4.47, Luc. Herm. 40 ; generally, of attendants on officials, μ. οἰκονόμου PTeb. 121.58 (i BC), cf. 179 (ii BC) ; ἄνδρας μ. PCair. Zen. 80.4 (iii BC).

opt. μαστιγοίην (v.l. -οῖμι) Aeschin. 2.157 ; fut. -ώσω X. Cyr. 1.4.13 ; aor. -ωσα Hdt. 7.54 ; — Pass., fut. μαστιγωθήσομαι LXX Ps. 72 (73).5, μαστιγώσομαι Pl. R. 361e, IG2². 1362.9 ; aor. part. -ωθείς Phld. Rh. 2.180 S. : — whip, flog, Hdt. 1.114 (μαστιγέων codd.), 3.16, 7.54 ; μυρίκῃ ἢ μαλάχῃ Luc. Ind. 3 ; — Pass., Lys. 1.18, etc. ; πληγὰς μαστιγούσθω let him be whipped, Pl. Lg. 914b, cf. 845a ; ψυχῆς ἠσκημένης καὶ μεμαστιγωμένης Max.Tyr. 25.5.
ον, that deserves whipping, Luc. Herod. 8.
εως, ἡ, whipping, flogging, Charicles ap. Ath. 8.350c (pl.).
α, ον, ἐστὶ μ. he must be whipped, Ar. Ra. 633.
ή, όν, gloss on μάστειρα, Sch. A. Supp. 163.
ἀκίδες ἢ ἀγκύλαι, Hsch.

Nonn. D. 2.645, Dor. μαστίσδω Theoc. 7.108 ; Ep. aor. μάστιξα Il. 5.768 ; — Pass., aor. ἐμαστίχθην v.l. in Hdt. 1.114 ; part. μαστιχθείς AP 9.348 (Leon. Alex.) ; (< μάστιξ) : — whip, flog, μάστιξεν δ’ ἵππους Il. l.c., etc. ; τυ… ὑπὸ… ὤμους μαστίσδοιεν (v. supr.) Theoc. l.c. ; c. inf., μάστιξεν δ’ ἐλάαν whipped them on or forward, Il. 5.366, Od. 6.82, etc. ; metaph, ἵνα… σε πολλοὶ μαστίξωσι λόγοις Epigr.Gr. 303.5 (Smyrna).
stimulate the bowels, Steph. in Hp. 2.311 D. ; — Pass., ib. 312 D. — Ep. word, used twice in Com., Eup. 72, Alex. 133.5, also in LXX Nu. 22.25, Wi. 5.11 (Pass.) ; and in late Prose, Plu. Alex. 42, Luc. Pr. Im. 24, etc. ; the Att. form being μαστιγόω.
ἡ, v. μάστειρα.
ορος, ὁ, scourger, A. Eu. 159 (lyr.).

ιγος, ἡ, whip, scourge, mostly for driving horses, Il. 5.748, etc. ; μ. λιγυρῇ 11.532 ; ἵππου μ. horse-whip, Hdt. 4.3 ; λιγυρὰ μ. διπλῆ S. Aj. 242 (anap.) ; later, scourge, ὑπὸ μαστίγων διαβαίνειν to cross under the lash, of soldiers flogged on, Hdt. 7.56, cf. 103 ; τοξεύειν ὑπὸ μ. X. An. 3.4.25 ; τῇ μ. κνάπτειν Cratin. 275 ; μάστιγ’ ἔχων whip in hand, Ar. Th. 933, Phryn.Com. 36. metaph, scourge, plague, μάστιξ Διός Il. 12.37, 13.812 ; μάστιγι θείᾳ… ἐλαύνομαι A. Pr. 682 ; πληγεὶς θεοῦ μάστιγι Id. Th. 608 ; διπλῇ μ., τὴν Ἄρης φιλεῖ, i.e. fire and sword, Id. Ag. 642 ; μ. [Θεοῦ], of sickness, Ev. Marc. 5.34, cf. 3.10 (pl.) ; but μάστιξ Πειθοῦς the lash of eloquence, Pi. P. 4.219 ; — Ion. μάστις ; μάστιγξ is not found.
τό, cup in the form of a breast, IG 7.3498.15, al. (Oropus).
ιος, ἡ, Ion. for μάστιξ, dat. μάστι Il. 23.500 ; acc. μάστιν Od. 15.182, AP 6.234 (Eryc.).
οῦ, ὁ, scourger, v.l. for ὑπασπιστής, LXX 4 Ma. 9.11.
τό, mastich-wine, Alex.Trall. 8.2.
gnash the teeth, Ep. dat. part. μαστιχόωντι Hes. Sc. 389 ; — Med., gloss on μασταρίζειν, Hsch.
τό, mastich-oil, Dsc. 1.42 (in lemmate).

ἡ, mastich, μ. τρώγειν Com.Adesp. 338 ; obtained from σχῖνος, mastich, Pistacia Lentiscus, or from ἰξίνη, pine-thistle, Atractylis gummifera, Thphr. HP 9.1.2, cf. Dsc. 1.70 ; the latter distd. as ἡ ἀκανθική Thphr. HP 6.4.9 ; used as a cosmetic, Luc. Ind. 23, Alex. 21.
(sc. ἔμπλαστρος), ἡ, a plaster, Aët. 15.15 (a) Z.
η, ον, prepared with mastich, ἔλαιον Dsc. 1.42, Gal. 11.870, Philagr. ap. Orib. 5.19.10.

poet. form of μαστίζω in pres. and impf., whip, scourge, μάστιε νῦν Il. 17.622, cf. Hes. Sc. 466, Pancrat. Oxy. 1085.15, Nonn. D. 1.179, al. ; — Med., οὐρῇ δὲ πλευράς τε καὶ ἰσχία ἀμφοτέρωθεν μαστίεται Il. 20.171.
ὁ, = μαστόδετον, Gal. 18(1).774.
τό, breast-band, AP 6.201 (pl., Marc. Arg.).

ές, like a breast, Arist. HA 529a18 ; πλακοῦς Sosib. ap. Ath. 3.115a ; λόφος μ. a small round hill, Plb. 5.70.6 ; πέτρα DS. 17.75 ; ἀποφύσεις mastoid processes, Gal. UP 11.20 ; ἐκφύσεις (in the womb) Diocl. Fr. 27.

ὁ, Ep., Ion. μαζός, Hom., Hdt. (exc. in 3.133, 5.18, where codd. give μαστός ; twice in codd. of Trag., A. Ch. 531, E. Ba. 701) ; Dor. μασδός Theoc. 3.16, 48 ; later μασθός LXX Is. 32.12 (cod. A), al., Asclep. ap. Gal. 13.934, Apoc. 1.13 (v.l.), IG 3.238 b, PMagLond. 121.208, etc., also in codd. of A. Ch. 545 ; — usage contradicts the statement of Gramm. that μαζός is the man΄s breast, μαστός the woman΄s ; — breast, δεξιτερὸν κατὰ μαζόν Il. 5.393 ; of men΄s breasts, βάλε δουρὶ στέρνον ὑπὲρ μαζοῖο 4.528 ; βάλε στῆθος παρὰ μαζόν 8.121, cf. Od. 22.82, X. An. 1.4.17, 4.3.6. more freq. of a woman΄s breast, μαζὸν ἀνέσχε, of Hecuba pleading with Hector, Il. 22.80 ; εἴ ποτέ τοι λαθικηδέα μαζὸν ἐπέσχον ib. 83 ; γυναῖκά τε θήσατο μαζόν sucked her breast, 24.58 ; πάϊς δέ οἱ ἦν ἐπὶ μαζῷ Od. 11.448 ; σὺ δέ μ’ ἔτρεφες… τῷ σῷ ἐπὶ μαζῷ 19.483 ; so φαίνουσαι τοὺς μαζούς Hdt. 2.85 ; τοὺς μ. ἀποταμοῦσα Id. 4.202 ; ἐπὶ τοῦ μαστοῦ ἔφυ φῦμα Id. 3.133 ; προὔκειτο μαστῶν περονίς S. Tr. 925 ; προσέσχε μαζόν, of the mother, A. Ch. 531 ; μαστὸν ἀμφέχασκε, of the child, ib. 545, cf. 897 ; μαστῶν ἀποστάς S. El. 776 ; πῶλον ἀφέλξων σῶν ἀπὸ μαστῶν E. Hec. 142 (anap.), etc. rarely of animals, udder, Id. Cyc. 55 (lyr.), 207, Call. Jov. 48. generally, of the breasts of all mammalia, Arist. HA 521b21, PA 688a18 sq., GA 752b23. metaph, any round, breast-shaped object; round hill, knoll, Pi. P. 4.8, X. An. 4.2.6, Call. Del. 48.
round piece of wool fastened to the edge of nets, X. Cyn. 2.6, cf. Poll. 5.29. at Paphos, breast-shaped cup, Apollod. Cyren. ap. Ath. 11.487b, cf. IG 7.3498 (Oropus), 11 (4).1307.21 (Delos).
Elean, = μαστρεία.
ἡ, Elean μαστράα Schwyzer 409.6 (v BC) ; — = εὔθυνα, IG 5(1).1433.15, 16 (pl., Messen., i AD) ; μαστρίαι· αἱ τῶν ἀρχόντων εὔθυναι, Hsch.
ή, όν, concerning μαστροί, νόμος SIG 671 A 5 (Delph., ii BC).
ἡ, pandering, X. Smp. 3.10, Plu. 2.632e.
= προαγωγεύω, τινα X. Smp. 4.57 ; μ. τινὰ πρὸς τὴν πόλιν seduce one into public life, ib. 8.42, cf. Luc. Tim. 16 ; metaph, αἰσθήσεις μ. ἡδονῇ Ph. 1.40.
ή, όν, ready to pander ; Adv. Sup. μαστροπικώτατα Sch. S. Aj. 520.
ίδος, ἡ, fem. of μαστροπός, Lib. Decl. 40.46 (pl.).

ὁ and ἡ, pimp or procuress, Ar. Th. 558, Diph. 43.22 (both fem.), Luc. Symp. 32 (masc.) ; metaph, X. Smp. 4.57 (masc.), Luc. Am. 16 (fem.). as Adj., μάστροπα ἔργα τελοῦντες, = μαστροπικοί, Man. 4.306.
ες, like a pander, λόγοι Sch. E. Hec. 826.

ὁ, = μαστήρ II, title of financial officials, at Pellene, Arist. Fr. 567 ; at Rhodes, IG 12(1).677.35 (iii BC), al., cf. Hsch. ; at Delphi, SIG 671 A 3 (ii BC). (Cf. μαίομαι.) at Olympia, SEG 31.358 (v BC).
ὁ, = μαστροπός, Hsch.
μαστρύλλιον, f. ll. for ματρυλεῖον.
v. ματρυλεῖον.
υος, ἡ, = μαστροπός, Phot. s.v. ματρυλεῖον.
ύος, ἡ, Ion. for μάστευσις, Call. Fr. 277.
ες, = μαστοειδής, Gloss.
ου, ὁ, = μασητήρ ; nickname of a parasite, Hsch.
κάνεον, πίναξ, Hsch. ; cf. μασχάλιον.

ἡ, arm-pit, ὑπὸ μασχάλῃ h.Merc. 242, etc. ; in pl., Ar. Ach. 852, Ec. 60 ; μασχάλην αἴρειν, = κωθωνίζεσθαι, Cratin. 298 ; οἰνωμένος μ. ἆραι Ael. Ep. 15 ; of animals, λύκοι νεβρὸν φέρουσιν ἀμφὶ μασχάλαις A. Fr. 39 ; μ. τῶν ἐμπροσθίων σκελῶν, of elephants, Arist. PA 688b5. in trees and plants, hollow at base of a shoot, axil, Thphr. CP 1.6.4 ; hence, branch, Id. HP 3.15.1.
young palm-twigs for making baskets or ropes, Hsch.
part of the olive-leaf, Id. ; of the leaf of ἀνδρόσαιμον, Dsc. 3.156.
bay, Str. 6.2.3.
corner, ἁβυβλίνα μ. Tab.Heracl. 1.92. in a ship, the part of the πρῷρα to which the ἀρτέμων is fastened, Hsch. part of a dirigible χελώνη, Ath.Mech. 34.5.
ὑπὸ κόλπον καὶ ὑπὸ μάλην φέρει, Hsch.
πλίνθος, corner-stone, IG1². 372.13, 98 ; φλέψ basilic vein, Paul.Aeg. 6.40, Steph. in Gal. 1.304D.

put under the arm-pits ; hence, mutilate a corpse, since murderers believed that by cutting off the extremities (nose, ears, etc.), stringing them together, and passing the string round the neck and under the arm-pits of the victim they would avert vengeance, A. Ch. 439 (lyr., Pass.), S. El. 445 (Pass.), cf. Ar.Byz. ap. Phot., Suid. s.v. μασχαλίσματα, EM 118.29, * 574.202, etc.
= μασχάλιον.
also μασχάλινον, τό, basket of palm-leaves, Hsch., Sch. Orib. 2.743 D. ; cf. μασχαλέον.
ίδος, ἡ, = μασχάλη II, Thphr. HP 3.7.5, Ctes. Fr. 57.28 (pl.). = μασχαλιστήρ I, Hsch.

τά, extremities cut off from a corpse, S. Fr. 623.
flesh of the shoulders, laid on the haunches at sacrifices, Hsch., Suid.
ὁ, mutilation, S. Fr. 623.

ῆρος, ὁ, girth passing round the horse behind his shoulders and fastened to the yoke by the λέπαδνον, Poll. 1.147, Hsch. generally, girth, band, A. Pr. 71, Hdt. 1.215 ; μ. ἔνλιθος CPR 22.5 (ii AD).
second dorsal vertebra, Poll. 2.178.
τὸν χιτῶνα, Hsch.

= ματάω, speak or work folly, S. OT 891 (lyr.) ; σπλάγχνα δ’ οὔ τι ματᾴζει my heart is not deceived, A. Ag. 995 (lyr.). — On the form cf. Hdn. Gr. 2.929, EM 737.21 ; — ματαΐζω, J. BJ 6.2.10, Suid. (ματᾴζω is prob. contr. fr. ματαιΐζω.)
= ματᾴζω, Epicur. Ep. 1 p. 22U. (v.l. -αιΐζ-), Ph. 1.222, al., Luc. Luct. 16, Palaeph. 10, S.E. M. 9.282 (v.l. ματάζω, i.e. ματᾴζω).
= ματᾴζω.
nugigerulus, Gloss.
ον, idly boasting, Sch. Ar. Ach. 589.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, = ματαιοπονία, prob. in Hp. Praec. 12.
talk idly, Str. 2.1.19, Aesop. 417, Hsch. s.v. ἐμματᾴζων, Suid. s.v. θαλαττοκοπεῖς.
ἡ, idle talk, Diogenian. Epicur. 2.16, 1 Ep. Ti. 1.6, Plu. 2.6f, Vett.Val. 150.24 (pl.), al., Porph. Abst. 4.16.
ον, talking at random, Telest. 1.9, Ep. Tit. 1.10, Vett.Val. 301.11.
v. ματιολοιχός.
= ματαιοπονέω, Herm. in Phdr. p. 66 A.
όν, acting foolishly, Ath. 5.179f.
labour in vain, Democr. 52, Plb. 9.2.2, 24.15.11, Aret. SD 1.12.
ατος, τό, work done in vain, Iamb. VP 5.24.
ἡ, labour in vain, Str. 17.1.28, Plu. 2.119e, Luc. DMort. 10.8.
ον, labouring in vain, τεχνίτης Ph. 2.500 ; ματαιοπόνον ἀποκαλεῖν τὴν φύσιν Gal. UP 5.5, cf. Apollon.Cit. 3.
= ματαιοπονέω, Eust. 543.4.
ἡ, = ματαιοπονία, Eust. 543.4.
ωνος, ὁ, having a beard in vain, Sch. Theoc. 14.28.

α, ον A. Pr. 331, Th. 442, Ag. 422 (lyr.), etc. ; also ος, ον ib. 1151, Ch. 82, Eu. 337 (all lyr.), S. OC 780, E. IT 628, Pl. Sph. 231b, D. 1.18 ; (< μάτη) : — vain, empty, idle ; of words, acts, etc., μάταια νομίζομεν Thgn. 141, cf. 487, 492, etc. ; μ. λόγοι idle tales or words, Hdt. 7.10. ηʹ ; μ. ἔπεα ib. 11 ; δόξαι φέρουσαι χάριν μ. A. Ag. 422 (lyr.) ; μ. ὑλάγματα, ποιφύγματα, ib. 1672, Th. 281 ; μ. εὐχή E. l.c. ; μάταια βάζειν τινά Id. Hipp. 119 ; μ. τι δρᾶσαί τινα Id. Cyc. 662 (lyr.) ; μ. ἂν εἴη πόνος Pl. Ti. 40d ; μ. ἡδονή S. l.c. ; δοξοσοφία Pl. Sph. l.c. ; ὄρεξις Arist. EN 1094a21 ; τὰ μ. ἀναλώματα useless expenses, POxy. 58.20 (iii AD) ; but also, μ. ἔπος a word of offence, Hdt. 3.120. of persons, empty, foolish, ματαιότεροι νόον Thgn. 1025, cf. Hdt. 2.173, S. Tr. 863, 888 (lyr.), Ar. V. 338, Amips. 9 (Sup.) ; φῦλον ματαιότατον Pi. P. 3.21 ; worthless, S. Ant. 1339 (lyr.).
rash, irreverent, profane, freq. in A., μ. γλῶσσα Pr. l.c., Ag. 1662 (troch.) ; φρονήματα Th. 438 ; αὐτουργίαι μ., of matricide and the like, Eu. l.c. ; χαρὰ μ. mad merriment, Th. 442 ; μ. ἀνοσίων τε κνωδάλων Supp. 762 ; τὸ μὴ μ. seriousness, gravity, ib. 198 ; ψαύειν ματαίαις χερσί S. Tr. 565. Adv. -ως idly, without ground, ib. 940, Emp. 39.2, E. Fr. 908.4 ; ὀχλεῖν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις Aen.Tact. 6.1 ; μ. ἐρεῖν to no purpose, Pl. Ep. 331d ; ταλαιπωρῆσαι Polystr. p. 31 W.
ἡ, = ματαιότης, Polem. Phgn. 13, al.
ον, having illegitimate children, gloss on ἀλιτόκαρπος, Hsch., EM 65.15.
ἡ, useless art, Quint. 2.20.3, Gal. Protr. 9 ; [pictura] apud veteres μ. dicta est, Serv. Dan. ad Verg. A. 1.464.
ητος, ἡ, vanity, purposelessness, ματαιότης ματαιοτήτων LXX Ec. 1.2, cf. Ph. 1.426 ; τῇ μ. ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη Ep. Rom. 8.20 ; folly, ἀνθρώπων Phld. Rh. 2.26 S.
όν, = ματαιοποιός, Ph. 2.98.
ον, = ματαιολόγος, Phot. s.v. λῆρος.
gloss on ματᾴζω, Sch. S. OT 891.
= κενοφροσύνη, Phot.
ὁ, ἡ, gen. φρονος, weak-minded, LXX 3 Ma. 6.11, Adam. 2.24.
ἡ, idle talk, Phot. and Suid. s.v. κενοφωνία.
ον, talking idly, Hsch. s.v. μαψίφωνος.

bring to naught, Sch. S. Tr. 258, Gloss. ματαιοῦσιν ἑαυτοῖς ὅρασιν invent a vision of their own, LXX Je. 23.16. more freq. in Pass., to be brought to naught, οὐ ματαιωθήσεται τὰ ῥήματα ib. Ju. 6.4.
become foolish, act foolishly, ἐματαιώθην σφόδρα ib. 1 Ch. 21.8, cf. Ep. Rom. 1.21 ; μεματαίωταί σοι thou hast done foolishly, LXX 1Ki. 13.13.
or ματᾳσμός, ὁ, = crepitus ventris, Pl.Com. 61 (pl.), Seleuc. ap. Ath. 2.76f (pl.).
v. sub μάταν².
v. sub μάταν².
Adv., Dor. for μάτην.
ἡ λύγξ, ἔνιοι δὲ ματακὸς ἢ ματακόν Hsch.
ἡ, v. μέταξα.
στέφανος μεμαρασμένος, Hsch. (fort. μαδαρός).
= ματαϊσμός.

(< μάτην) ; — poet. Verb, to be idle, dally, ἀπέκοψε παρήορον οὐδὲ μάτησε Il. 16.474, cf. 23.510 ; μὴ τὼ μὲν (sc. ἵππω) δείσαντε ματήσετον 5.233 ; οὐ ματᾷ τοὔργον the work lags not, goes on apace, A. Pr. 57 ; ματᾶν ὁδῷ to loiter by the way, Id. Th. 37 ; ἰδώμεθ΄, εἴ τι τοῦδε φροιμίου ματᾷ is in vain, is fruitless, Id. Eu. 142 ; of persons, fail of a thing, τινος Oppian. H. 3.102.
οῦ, ὁ, = μαστευτής, κακεμπορίης Man. 4.268.

fut. -σω Il. 14.110 ; aor. ἐμάτευσα Pi. O. 5.24 ; — = μαστεύω, abs., seek, search, ἐγγὺς ἀνήρ, οὐ δηθὰ ματεύσομεν Il. l.c. ; οἴκοθεν μάτευε Pi. N. 3.31, cf. S. OC 211 (lyr.). c. acc., seek for, search after, ματεύει ὧν ἀνευρήσει φόνον A. Ag. 1094, cf. Ch. 219, S. Ph. 1210 (lyr.), Ichn. 13, etc. ; θάνατον εὑρέμεν μ. ἐλάφῳ Simon. 30 (cj.). c. inf., seek, strive to do, μὴ ματεύσῃ θεὸς γενέσθαι Pi. O. 5.24, cf. S. OT 1052. c. acc. loci, search, explore, ματεύει ἄλλος ἀλλοίαν κέλευθον B. 9.35 ; πάντα Ar. Th. 663 ; τὰ χωρία Theoc. 21.65.

ἡ, folly, fault, μάτας εἰπών speaking folly, Stesich. 47, cf. A. Ch. 918 (pl.) ; μάταισι πολυθρόοις with clamorous lewdness, Id. Supp. 820 (lyr.) (but expld. by Sch. as ΄quest΄) ; οὔ τί τοι μέτρον μάτας S. Fr. 798. cf. μάτην ad fin.
*μάτημι, Aeol., = ματεύω, in 2 sg. pres. μάτης, ἐξ ἑτέρω ἕτερον μ. Theoc. 29.15 ; — Pass., Ion. ματεῖσθαι, = ζητεῖσθαι, Hp. ap. Erot. (Hsch. has ματεῖ· ζητεῖ.)
*μάτημι, Aeol., = πατέω, Alc. Supp. 31.3 ; pres. part. fem. μάτεισαι Sappho 54.

[ᾰ] Dor. μάτᾱν, Adv. in vain, h.Cer. 308, Pi. O. 1.83, etc. ; μὴ πόνει μ. A. Pr. 44 ; βλέποντες ἔβλεπον μ. ib. 447 ; μ. ἐρεῖν ib. 1007 ; with a Noun, τὸ μ. ἄχθος the fruitless burden, Id. Ag. 165 (lyr.) ; Διὸς μ. ἄκοιτις his bedfellow to no good end, S. Tr. 1149 ; as predicate, μ. ὁ μόχθος A. Ch. 521.
at random, without reason, οὔ σε μ. τιμῶσι Thgn. 523 ; ὅρα μὴ μ. κόμπος ὁ λόγος ᾖ Hdt. 7.103, cf. E. Supp. 127 ; οὐ γὰρ δίκαιον… τοὺς κακοὺς μ. χρηστοὺς νομίζειν S. OT 609 ; ἵνα μὴ μ. θαρρήσῃς Pl. Tht. 189d ; ὁ νοσῶν μ., i.e. he that is mad, S. Aj. 635 (lyr.), cf. Ar. Pax 95 (anap.).
idly, falsely, λέγοντες εἴτ’ ἀληθές, εἴτ’ ἄρ’ οὖν μ. S. Ph. 345 ; λόγῳ μάτην θνῄσκοντες Id. El. 63, cf. 1298 ; μ. βέβακεν, of a dream, A. Ag. 423 (lyr.). — Originally acc. of μάτη, and we find εἰς μάτην in Luc. Trag. 28, 241, Aristid. Or. 33 (51).3 ; ἐπὶ μ. POxy. 530.8 (ii AD).
(< ματήρ) = ματεύω, Hsch., Phot.
ἡ, Dor. for μήτηρ.
ῆρος, ὁ, = μαστήρ, Hsch.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, (< μάτη) vain attempt, bootless enterprise, ἡμετέρῃ ματίῃ Od. 10.79.
folly, error, ARh. 1.805, 4.367.
v. sub μάτιον.
= ματεύω, in aor. inf. ματίσαι, Hsch. (leg. ματῆσαι).

ὁ (on the accent v. Hdn. Gr. 1.231), Ar. Nu. 451, expld. as = κρουσιμέτρης, from μάτιον, τό, trifle, scrap, by Sch. ad loc. ; ματαιολοιχός· ὁ περὶ τὰ μικρὰ πανοῦργος καὶ λίχνος, Hsch. ; — Bentley cj. ματτυολοιχός (in both places), v. ματτύη.
τό, trifle, scrap, by Sch. ad Ar. Nu. 451.
τό, Egyptian measure of capacity, Arch.Pap. 5.178 No.32, Ostr. 296 (ii AD), al., PTeb. 314.18 (ii AD), PLond. 5.1906 (vi AD), prob. in PAmh. 2.130.5 (i AD) ; hence ματιαῖον μέτρον Sammelb. 4683.6.
τό, or ὁ, search, Hp. ap. Gal. 19.120.
Dor. etc. for μητραδελφεός.
Dor. etc. for μητρόδοκος.
Dor. etc. for μητρόθεν.
Dor. for μητροκασιγνήτη.
Dor. for μητρομήτωρ.
Dor. etc. for μητρόξενος.
Dor. for μητρόπολις.
Dor. for μητροπόλος.
Dor. for μητρόρριπτος.
Dor. etc. for μητρυιά.
τό, brothel, Din. Fr. 43.5, Men. Epit. 429, Plu. 2.752c ; written ματρύλλιον or μαστρύλλιον ib. 1094a, Poll. 6.188.
v. ματρυλεῖον.
ὁ, fem. μάτρυλλα, ἡ, pimp, Phryn. PS p. 84B., Eust. 380.5.
Dor. for μητρῳασμός.
Dor. for μήτρων.
Dor. for μητρῷος.
Dor. for μήτρως.
περιβλέπει, ἀδημονεῖ, Hsch.
ἀπορῶν, Hsch.
μέλλων καὶ ἀποκνῶν, Hsch.
ον, = μωρός, Hsch.
eat or dress a ματτύη, Alex. 49.

(not -ύα), ἡ, Nicostr.Com. 8, Sophil. 4.5, Macho 1 ; but ματτύης, ου, ὁ, Artem. ap. Ath. 14.663d ; gender doubtful in Philem. 9, 12, Alex. 205 : — a rich, highly-flavoured dish, made of hashed meat, poultry, and herbs, and served cold as a dessert, of Macedonian or Thessalian origin, cf. Poll. 6.70 (ματύλλη codd.). — Especially freq. in the New Comedy acc. to Ath. 14.662f ; but ματτυολοιχός is prob. cj. for ματιολοιχός.
ου, ὁ, v. ματτύη.
ου, ὁ, a nickname, = ματτυολοιχός, Amm. Marc. 15.55.4.
(cj.), v. ματτύη
λαοτομίον, Hsch.
dub.sens. in Hdn. Gr. 1.142.
τὸ χλιαρόν, Hsch.
ἡ, v. μαῦλις.
= μαστροπεύω, Hsch. s.v. μαστροπός, Sch. Ar. Nu. 976.
ἡ, knife, acc. μαῦλιν Call. Aet. 3.1.9 ; dat. μαύλιδι Nic. Th. 706 ; nom. pl. μαύλιες AP 15.25 (Besant.) ; — also μαυλία, ἡ, in acc. pl. -ίας, Sch. Th. 1.6, Suid.
ιδος, or ιος, ἡ, bawd, procuress, Hsch.
τό, bawd΄s hire, Hippon. 126 ; but also, brothel, PLond. 5.1877.7 (vi AD).
οῦ, ὁ, = μαστροπός, Cat.Cod.Astr. 8(4).212, Phot. and Suid. s. h. v. ; fem. μαυλίστρια, EM 695.31, Sch. Ar. Nu. 976, Suid. s.v. πυγοστόλος.
όν, = ἀμαυρός, Hdn. Gr. 1.193 (μαῦρος codd.) ; μαῦρος Hsch. ; cited (without transl.) as properisp. by Gal. 18(2).518.

= ἀμαυρόω, darken, blind ; hence, make powerless, dub. in A. Eu. 358 (lyr.), cj. in Pi. I. 4 (3).48. metaph, make dim or obscure, ῥεῖα δέ μιν μαυροῦσι θεοί Hes. Op. 325 ; — Pass., become dim or obscure, Thgn. 192, A. Ag. 296.

SIG 167.2, al. (Mylasa, iv BC), or Μαύσωλλος, ib. 169.3 (Iasos, iv BC), or Μαύσωλος (as freq. in codd.), ὁ, Mausolus, a Carian noble, Hdt. 5.118 ; another, called satrap or king, X. Ages. 2.26, D. 15.3, SIG ll.cc., etc. ; — Adj. Μαυσσώλλειος or Μαυσσώλλεος, τετράδραχμα IG 11(2).161 B 21, al. (Delos, iii BC) ; Μαυσώλεῖον, τό, tomb of M. at Halicarnassus, Plin. HN 36.30 ; — hence, as appellat., mausoleum, Str. 5.3.8, Paus. 8.16.4 (pl.).
= Μαύσσωλλος.
τό, = μαφόρτης, BGU 948.19 (iv/v AD), Sammelb. 7033.39 (v AD).
ου, ὁ, veil, head-dress of women and priests (cf. Gloss.), BGU 845.15 (ii AD), etc. ; also, = peplus, ricinus, Gloss. ; Dim. μαφόρτιον, τό, POxy. 1295.19 (ii/iii AD), PMeyer 23.6 (iv AD), etc.

ας (later -ης, dat. -ῃ, PTeb. 16.14 (ii BC), Ev. Luc. 21.24, etc.), ἡ, large knife or dirk, Il. 11.844, 18.597, 19.252 ; μ. ἥ οἱ πὰρ ξίφεος μέγα κουλεὸν αἰὲν ἄωρτο 3.271 ; carving-knife, Pi. O. 1.49, Hdt. 2.61, Ar. Eq. 489, Pl. R. 353a, etc. ; κοπίδες μ. E. Cyc. 242 ; sacrificial knife, Ar. Pax 948, Pl.Com. 91, Michel 832.52 (Samos, iv BC) ; — ἡ Δελφικὴ μ. a knife adapted to various purposes, Arist. Pol. 1252b2, cf. Hsch. s.v. Δελφικὴ μ. ; prov., of greedy persons, because Delphian sacrificers claimed a share for the knife, App. prov. 1.94. as a weapon, short sword, dagger, Pi. N. 4.59, Hdt. 6.75, 7.225, Lys. 13.87, etc. ; an assassin΄s weapon, Antipho 5.69 ; used by jugglers, Pl. Euthd. 294e (pl.), etc. ; later, sabre, opp. the straight sword (< ξίφος), X. Eq. 12.11, cf. HG 3.3.7, Cyr. 1.2.13, Ev. Matt. 26.52, etc. ; οἱ ἐπὶ τῆς μ., of a bodyguard, Arr. Epict. 1.30.7 ; but, ἐπὶ μ. τασσόμενοι possessing power of life and death (jus gladii), Cat.Cod.Astr. 8(4).173 ; μ. ἱππική cavalry sabre, IG 11(2).161 B 99 (Delos, iii BC). μ. κουρίδες, shears or scissors, Cratin. 37 ; κεκαρμένος μοιχὸν μιᾶ μ., i.e. with one blade, Ar. Ach. 849, cf. Poll. 2.32 (where διπλῇ is f.l.), Hsch. s.v. μιᾷ μαχαίρᾳ· μ. κουρικαί Plu. Dio 9. metaph, διὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ πυρός Zen. 3.19, cf. Posidipp. 1.10 ; μ. τοῦ πνεύματος Ep. Eph. 6.17, cf. LXX Is. 49.2. name of a precious stone, Arist. Mir. 847a5, Ps.-Plu. Fluv. 10.5. part of the liver, Ruf. Onom. 180.
ᾶ, ὁ, cutler, POxy. 1676.6 (iii AD).
τό, Dim. of μάχαιρα, Ph. 2.530 (pl.), Luc. Pisc. 45.

τό, = μαχαιρίδιον, X. An. 4.7.16, Men. 765, PEleph. 5.13 (iii BC), Str. 12.2.10 ; surgeon΄s or barber΄s knife, Hp. Medic. 6, 7, Arist. GA 789b13, Metaph. 1061a4, Com.Adesp. 327, Plu. Brut. 13, Ruf. Ren. Ves. 12.12.
ίδος, ἡ, butcher΄s cleaver, Ar. Eq. 412 ; knife, μικρὰ μ. Plu. Art. 19, cf. Luc. Ind. 29 ; dagger, Str. 16.4.17 ; pl., shears, scissors, ὁ κουρεὺς τὰς μ. λαβών Eup. 278, cf. Poll. 10.140.
ωνος, ὁ, = ξιφίον, Dsc. 4.20 ; v.l. μαχαιρώνιον.
ή, όν, = μαχαιρωτός, καυτήρ v.l. in Paul.Aeg. 6.62.
ου, ὁ, sword-belt, Hsch.
ἡ, case for knives, Michel 832.52 (Samos, iv BC).
[οπέω], cut with a μάχαιρα, dub. in UPZ 119.40 (ii BC).
fight with a μάχαιρα, Plb. 10.20.3 ; — Subst. μαχαιρομαχία, gloss on ξιφιστύς, Hsch.
v. μαχαιρομαχέω.
τό, cutler΄s factory, D. 27.31.
ὁ, maker of cutlery, Ar. Av. 442, D. 27.9, Plu. Dem. 4, Luc. Rh. Pr. 10.
= μαχαιροπώλιον.
ου, ὁ, cutler, Poll. 7.156.
or μαχαιροπωλεῖον, τό, cutler΄s shop, Plu. Dem. 15, Poll. l.c.
όν, = μαχαιροποιός, Tz. H. 6.132.
ἡ, sword-bearing, wearing of arms, Wilcken Chr. 13.9 (i AD).
wear a sabre, J. AJ 18.2.4, BJ 3.5.5.

ον, wearing a sabre, of Egyptians, Hdt. 9.32 ; μ. ἔθνος, of Persians, A. Pers. 56 (anap.) ; of Thracians, Th. 2.96, 7.27 ; — as Subst., swordsman, Plb. 38.7.2, Plu. Sull. 8, etc. ; freq. of military police in Egypt, PAmh. 2.38 (ii BC), PTeb. 35.13 (ii BC), OGI 737.6 (ii BC), Sammelb. 46, Ostr. Bodl. iii 64, etc.
τό, = gladiolus, prob. in Gloss.
v. μαχαιρίων.
ή, όν, sabre-shaped, πρίων Gal. 18(2).331, cf. Paul.Aeg. 6.62.
v. μαχητής.
Dor. for μηχανή.
Dor. for μηχάνησις.
ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Chalcedon, SIG 1011.7 (iii/ii BC).
ῆος, ὁ, title of Zeus at Cos, SIG 1026.10 (iv/iii BC) ; at Tanagra, IG 7.548 ; at Argos, SIG 56.29 (v BC), Paus. 2.22.2. (sc. μήν), month at Corcyra, IG 9(1).694.
ίδος, ἡ, title of Athena at Cos, SIG 1026.21 (iv/iii BC).
ιδος, ἡ, title of Aphrodite and Athena at Megalopolis, Paus. 8.31.6, 8.36.5.

Dor., v. μηχάνωμα.
crane, SIG 241 A 12 (pl.), al.
v. μαχητής.
Dor. for μαχητής.
(< μάχη) wish to fight, Hsch.
Ep. = μάχομαι.
Ion. = μάχομαι.
one must fight, Arist. Rh. 1403a9 (v.l. μαχητέον), Plu. 2.181c.

ἡ, (< μάχομαι) battle, combat, freq. in Hom., usu. of armies, μ. καὶ φύλοπις Il. 13.789 ; ἐπὶ ἶσα μ. τέτατο πτόλεμός τε 12.436 ; μ. ἐνοπή τε 12.35 ; μάχαι τ’ ἀνδροκτασίαι τε 7.237 ; sts. of single combat, ib. 158, 232, 263 ; μ. καὶ δηϊοτής ib. 290 ; ναῶν ἐν μάχαις Pi. N. 9.34 ; μάχαις καὶ ναυμαχίαις Lys. 30.26 ; μάχη δορός A. Ag. 439 (lyr.), etc. ; with Verbs, μάχην μάχεσθαι fight a battle, Il. 15.414, etc. ; θήσονται μ. 24.402 ; μάχας εἰσήλυθον 2.798 ; ἀρτύνθη μ. 11.216 ; μ. ἤγειραν 17.261 ; μ. ὀρνύμεν, ὤτρυνον, 9.353, 12.277 ; συμφερόμεσθα μάχῃ 11.736 ; πειρᾶτο μάχας Pi. N. 1.43 ; ἀντιάζειν τινὶ μάχαν ib. 67 ; σὺν γυναιξὶ τὰς μ. ποιούμενος S. El. 302, cf. X. Cyr. 3.3.29 ; μάχην συνάψαι ἐμβολαῖς A. Pers. 336 ; μ. συμβάλλειν τινί engage battle with…, E. Ba. 837 ; διὰ μάχης τινὶ ἀπικέσθαι, ἔρχεσθαι, ἥκειν, Hdt. 1.169, 6.9, A. Supp. 475 ; διὰ μάχης ἐκβαλεῖν τινα Arist. Pol. 1303a35 (so ἐξέπεσον διὰ μάχης ib. 34) ; εἰς μάχην πρός τινα ἐλθεῖν, μολεῖν, E. Ba. 636 (troch.), Ph. 694 ; ἐς μάχην ἐπεξιέναι τινί Th. 2.23 ; μάχης γενομένης Pl. Lg. 869c ; μάχῃ κρατῆσαι conquer in battle, E. HF 612, D. 18.193 (with v.l. μάχην)· νενικήκαμεν τὴν μεγάλην μ. X. Cyr. 7.5.53 ; Μιλτιάδης ὁ τὴν ἐν Μαραθῶνι μ. τοὺς βαρβάρους νικήσας Aeschin. 3.181 ; μάχη τινός battle with an enemy, Αἴαντος δ’ ἀλέεινε μ. Il. 11.542, cf. Hes. Sc. 361 ; μ. ὑπέρ τινος Pi. N. 7.42 ; περί τι Pl. Lg. 919b ; pl., strifes, ἔρις τε… πόλεμοί τε μάχαι τε Il. 1.177 ; μάχας ἐν λόγοις ποιεῖσθαι Pl. Ti. 88a, etc. ; generally, contention, strife, Id. Ep. 352c, etc. ; μάχης ἐάν τις ἄρξηται SIG 1109.72 (ii AD) ; μ. νομικαί Ep. Tit. 3.9. = ἀγών, contest, as for a prize in the games, Pi. O. 8.58 (but ἄεθλα, opp. μάχαι πολέμου, Id. O. 2.44).
struggle, μηχανή τε πολλὴ καὶ μ. ἦν περί τινος X. Cyr. 7.5.38.
mode of fighting, way of battle, ἡ μ. σφέων ἦν ἀπ’ ἵππων Hdt. 1.79 ; ἐπίστασθαι τὴν μ. τινῶν Id. 7.9. αʹ, cf. 7.85, X. Cyr. 2.1.7.
field of battle, interpol. in Id. An. 2.2.6, 5.55.4. in Logic, contradiction, inconsistency, Epict. Ench. 52.1, S.E. M. 7.392.
ον, gen. ονος, warlike, Il. 12.247 ; βῶλος, of the soil of Colchis, AP 4.3b. 22 (Agath.).
to battle, Theoc. 25.136.
one must fight, Mnesim. 7, Plu. Pomp. 32.

οῦ, ὁ, Aeol. μαχαίτας Alc. 33 ; Dor. μαχατάς Pi. N. 2.13, etc. ; Lacon. μαχατάρ (μαχάταρ cod.) Hsch. ; (< μάχη) : — fighter, warrior, μικρὸς μὲν ἔην δέμας ἀλλὰ μ. Il. 5.801 ; θείειν ταχὺς ἠδὲ μ. Od. 3.112 ; Τρῶάς φασι μ. ἔμμεναι ἄνδρας 18.261 ; φὼς μ. Pi. N. l.c. ; as Adj., μαχατὰν θυμὸν αἰσχυνθῆμεν his warrior heart, ib. 9.26 ; in later Prose, LXX Jo. 6.3, al.

ή, όν, fit for fighting, ὀδόντες μ. Arist. PA 662b34 ; warlike, μ. παιδιαί Id. Rh. 1371a1 ; of persons, pugnacious, ib. 1381a32, etc. ; μ. περὶ κέρδους ib. 1372b31 ; ἡ μαχητική (sc. τέχνη), skill in fighting, Pl. Sph. 225a ; τὸ μαχητικόν ibid. ; μ. ἵπποι restive horses, Id. R. 467e. Adv. -κῶς pugnaciously, Id. Tht. 168b ; in a hostile manner, μ. διακείμενα Simp. in Cael. 197.9.
ή, όν, to be fought with, κακὸν ἄγριον οὐδὲ μ. Od. 12.119.

η, ον, also ος, ον Hdt. 7.185 ; (< μάχη) : — fit for battle, warlike, ἐπειδὴ μ. εἶ since you΄re a fighting man, Ar. Av. 1368 ; αἱ μάχιμοι μυριάδες Hdt. l.c. ; τὸ μ. the effective force, Th. 6.23, X. Cyr. 5.44.46 ; τὸ τῆς πόλεως μ. Pl. Lg. 830c (but ἀνέωνται ἐς τὸ μ. = ἐς πόλεμον Hdt. 2.165) ; μ. γένη Pl. Mx. 240a ; τὸ μ. γένος Id. Ti. 24a, cf. Arist. Pol. 1268a36 ; τὸ μ. (sc. ἔθνος) Pl. Criti. 110c ; esp. in Egypt, οἱ μ. τῶν Αἰγυπτίων the warrior caste, Hdt. 2.141, cf. 164 ; so later, of native troops, freq. in Pap., PTeb. 61 (a).109 (ii BC), etc. ; Comp. -ώτερος Plb. 2.22.6 ; Sup. -ώτατος Hdt. 3.102, Ar. Ach. 153, Th. 1.110 ; τὰ μ. τῶν ἔργων Philostr. Her. 2.19. Adv. -μως Arr. Epict. 2.9.5. = μαχιμώδης, Gloss. disputable, S.E. M. 8.45.
ες, quarrelsome, AP 12.200 (Strat.).
άδος, poet. fem. of μάχλος (also late Prose, Ph. 1.40, al., Artem. 4.11), Man. 4.357, AP 5.104 (Marc. Arg.), 301.2 (Agath.) ; of things, wanton, luxuriant, ἐλπίς ib. 9.443 (Paul. Sil.).
to be lewd, in pf. part. Pass., μεμαχλευμένον ἦτορ Man. 4.315.
ου, ὁ, = μάχλος, Hsch. ; — fem. μαχλίς, Id.
ή, όν, like a μάχλος, Man. 4.184.
fem. of μάχλης.
τοὺς αὐτομόλους Αἰθίοπας, Hsch.
κρομμύων, Hsch.

ον, lewd, lustful, of women (λάγνος being used of men), μαχλόταται δὲ γυναῖκες Hes. Op. 586, cf. Ephor. 96 J. ; μ. ἐς ἄνδρας Aeschrio 8.6, cf. Ach.Tat. 8.1 ; of a man, Luc. Alex. 11 ; of Ἡδονή personified, Ph. 2.267. metaph, wanton, luxuriant, ἄμπελος A. Fr. 325.
wanton, insolent, Ἄρης Id. Supp. 636 (lyr.).
ἡ, lewdness, lust, of Paris, Il. 24.30 (rejected by Aristarch. as a word peculiar to women, but used of Paris as effeminate), cf. Hes. Fr. 28, Hdt. 4.154, Adam. 1.10, AP 5.301.10 (Agath.).
ητος, ἡ, = μαχλοσύνη, EM 594.24, Sch. Lyc. 771.

Ion. pres. opt. μαχέοιτο Il. 1.272, μαχέοιντο ib. 344 (v.l. μαχέονται) ; part. μαχεόμενος v.l. in Hdt. 7.104 (elsewh. μαχόμενος, 9.75, al.) ; Ep. μαχειόμενος Od. 17.471, μαχεούμενος 11.403, 24.113 ; Ep. impf. μαχέσκετο Il. 7.140 ; fut. μαχήσομαι 23.621, Hdt. 7.209 ; μαχέσομαι, διαμαχεσόμεθα (as v.l.) Id. 9.48 ; also in late Prose, J. AJ 11.8.3, Plu. 2.215f ; μαχοῦμαι S. OC 837, Ar. Pl. 1076, etc., μαχεῖται even in Il. 20.26, but μαχέονται 2.366 ; Ep. μαχέσσομαι v.l. for μαχήσομαι 1.298 ; aor. ἐμαχεσάμην Hdt. 1.18, etc. ; opt. μαχέσαιο Il. 6.329 ; inf. μαχέσασθαι 17.178, also μαχέσσασθαι 15.633 ; opt. μαχεσσαίμεσθα Theoc. 22.74 ; part. μαχεσσαμένω Il. 1.304 ; later μαχήσασθαι Paus. 1.27.1, (ἀνα-) DS. 19.93 ; pf. μεμάχημαι Th. 7.43, Lys. 7.41, Isoc. 6.54 ; late aor. ἐμαχέσθην Plu. 2.970f, Paus. 5.44.9 ; fut. μαχεσθήσομαι only Sch. rec. A. Th. 672 : — fight, Hom., etc. ; ὑσμῖνι μ. Il. 2.863 ; πολεμίζειν ἠδὲ μ. ib. 452, etc. ; μάχην μ. X. Ages. 5.5 ; in Hom. mostly of armies and persons fighting as parts of armies, but sts. of single combat, Il. 3.91, 433, 7.51, 111, 279, Od. 18.31, 39 ; between men and beasts, Il. 15.633, Od. 20.15 ; between beasts, Il. 16.824 ; — Constr. ; c. dat. pers., fight with, i.e. against, one, ἀνδράσιν ἶφι μ. Il. 1.151, cf. S. Ph. 1253, etc. ; μ. ἀντία, ἐναντίον τινός, Il. 20.88, 97 ; ἐπί τινι 5.124, etc. ; πρός τινα 17.471, but πρὸς δαίμονα against heaven΄s will, ib. 98 (in Att. Prose, mostly c. dat. or πρός, μ. τοῖς πολεμίοις D. 4.47 ; πρὸς ἀλλήλους Isoc. 4.116) ; μ. σὺν σοί,… θεά, with thy help, Od. 13.390 ; μετὰ πρώτοισι μ. among the foremost, Il. 5.575 ; μετὰ Βοιωτῶν μ. with them, in their ranks, 13.700 ; πρός τινας μετ’ ἀλλήλων Isoc. 10.53, cf. Pl. Smp. 179a ; κατὰ σφέας γὰρ μαχέονται will fight by themselves, Il. 2.366 (but κατ’ ἕνα μ. fight in single combat, Hdt. 7.104) ; μ. πρό τινος before him ; hence, metaph, for him, in his defence, Il. 4.156, 8.56, X. HG 5.44.33, etc. ; ὑπὲρ τοῦ νόμου Heraclit. 44 ; πάτρας ὕπερ E. Ph. 1002 ; Ἕλλησιν ὑπὲρ Ἑλλήνων Pl. Mx. 239b ; περὶ δαιτί Od. 2.245 ; but later usu. περί τινος, A. Supp. 740, Cratin. 163, Hdt. 1.95 ; ἀμφί τινι Il. 3.70, 91 ; ἀμφὶ νέκυι 16.565 ; εἵνεκά τινος 2.377 ; c. dat. instrum., τόξοισι, πελέκεσσι μ., 7.140, 15.711 (χερσὶ μαχέσσασθαι, of boxers, Od. 18.39) ; μ. ἀπ’ ἵππου fight from horseback, Hdt. 9.63 ; τὸ μήπω μεμαχημένον the force that had not yet come into action, Th. 7.43. c. acc., fight against, only f.l. in Philostr. Im. 2.23. generally, quarrel, wrangle, ἔριδι μ. Il. 1.8 ; μ. ἐπέεσσιν ib. 304, etc. ; τινι 5.875, 13.118 ; τῷ παιδὶ μ. make a scene with…, Thphr. Char. 23.8 ; dispute, argue, περί τι μ. Pl. R. 342d, etc.
contend for the mastery in games, etc., πὺξ μ. Il. 23.621 ; measure oneself with or against, τινι 1.272 ; παγκράτιον μ. Ar. V. 1190, 1195 ; μ. Ὀλυμπιάδα Philostr. Gym. 21. after Hom., struggle against a force, ἀνάγκᾳ δ’ οὐδὲ θεοὶ μ. Simon. 5.21 ; ὄμβρῳ Alc. Supp. 26.4 ; πρὸς ἡνίας μ. A. Pr. 1010 ; πρὸς ἐπιθυμίας ἢ ἡδονάς Pl. La. 191e ; μ. τῷ λιμῷ, τῷ δίψει, X. Cyr. 3.1.5. c. inf., struggle, make an effort to do, Arist. HA 552a23. of arguments, propositions, etc., to be in contradiction or inconsistent, τρία ὁμολογήματα μ. αὐτὰ αὑτοῖς Pl. Tht. 155b, cf. Plb. 16.28.4 ; μαχόμενα Phld. Mus. p. 95 K., S.E. P. 1.198, al.
Adv. self-contradictorily, Str. 2.1.40, S.E. M. 1.281, Iamb. Myst. 1.18.
a bird, Hdn. Gr. 1.404. [ᾱ by nature.]

Adv. in vain, without result, μ. οὕτω… πολεμίζειν Il. 2.120 ; without aim or object, 20.298.
vainly, falsely, μ. ὀμόσαιμι 15.40 ; μ. αὔτως εὐχετάασθαι 20.348 ; thoughtlessly, recklessly, σῖτον ἔδοντας μ. αὔτως Od. 16.111 ; μ. ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κόσμον Il. 2.214, 5.759 ; in haste, Od. 3.138. — Ep. word, in compds. Poet., mostly Ep.
ῶν, αἱ, (< αὔρα) random breezes, gusts of wind, Hes. Th. 872, cf. Call. Fr. 67 (al. divisim μὰψ αὖραι ἐπιπνείουσι θάλασσαν). as Adj., μαψαῦραι στόβοι idle boastings, Lyc. 395.

ον (also η, ον, v. infr.), (μάψ) vain, false, τὸ δ’ ἐμὸν ὄνομα… μαψίδιον ἔχει φάτιν E. Hel. 251 (lyr.) ; γλῶσσα μ. Theoc. 25.188 ; useless, worthless, μαψιδίη κόνις AP 7.602 (Agath.). in Hom. only Adv. μαψιδίως, = μάψ, thoughtlessly, at random, Il. 5.374, al. ; without reason, κεχολῶσθαι Od. 7.310 ; rashly, recklessly, 2.58, 14.365 ; μ. ἀλάλησθε, of pirates, 3.72.
ον, idly talking, μ. οἰωνοί birds whose cries convey no sure omen, h.Merc. 546.
ον, bringing forth in vain, λαγόνες AP 14.125 (Metrod.).
ον, = μαψιλόγος, Hsch.
α, ὁ, (< ὑλάω, ὑλακτῶ) idly barking, i.e. repeating a thing again and again, Pi. N. 7.105 ; μαψυλάκαν γλῶσσαν (fem.) prob. for μαψυλάκταν in Sappho 27.
μάταιος, Hsch.
*μάω, v. μαίομαι, μέμονα, μῶμαι.
ου, ὁ, = μεγαλοβρεμέτης, ποταμός Orph. A. 749.

ὁ, a Persian pr. n. (Hdt. 3.70, al.) and later title of generals and priests, Bagabukhša, lit. ΄set free by God΄, Hdt. 3.153, al., SIG 282.2 (Priene, iv BC), X. An. 5.3.6, Str. 14.1.23, App. BC 5.9, Hsch., etc. ; — hence μεγαβύξειοι λόγοι, boastings, Id. (Usu. -βυζ- in codd., as Str., App., and Hsch. ll.cc., but -βυξ- in SIG l.c., v.l. in Hdt. 3.153, 160, al., -bux- Quint. 5.12.21 codd., -byx- Plin. HN 35.93 codd. opt.)
ὁ, big toe, Orib. ap. Aët. 11.35.
ον, = μεγαλόδωρος, ἄρουρα Opp. C. 3.29.
ές, greatly astounded, Opp. C. 2.488.
ές, very bold, Hes. Sc. 385, Man. 2.372.
τό, Ion. for μέγεθος, Hdt.
ον, great-hearted, Ἀχιλλεύς Il. 20.498, cf. Hes. Th. 734, etc. ; Ἀχαιοί Il. 1.123, al. ; Ἀθήνη Od. 8.520, 13.121, cf. Orac. ap. Phleg. Fr. 36.3 J. ; ταῦρος Il. 16.488.
ον, illustrious, B. 1.44, 3.64.

aor. ἐμέγηρα, (from μέγας, cf. γεραίρω from γεραρός (< γέρας) prop. regard as too great ; hence, grudge one a thing as too great for him, μέγηρε γάρ οἱ τό γ’ Ἀπόλλων Il. 23.865 ; ἐγὼ δέ τοι οὔ τι μεγαίρω Orac. ap. Hdt. 1.66. c. inf. pro acc. rei, μηδὲ μεγήρῃς ἡμῖν εὐχομένοισι τελευτῆσαι τάδε ἔργα grudge us not the accomplishment…, Od. 3.55, cf. h.Merc. 465 ; c. acc. et inf., μνηστῆρας… οὔ τι μεγαίρω ἔρδειν ἔργα βίαια I complain not that…, Od. 2.235 ; ὃν οὐδέ κεν αὐτὸς ἀείδειν Φοῖβος… μεγαίροι Theoc. 7.101 ; c. inf. only, ἀμφὶ δὲ νεκροῖσιν κατακαιέμεν οὔ τι μεγαίρω I object not to [your] burning them, Il. 7.408 ; with inf. understood, τάων οὔ τοι ἐγὼ πρόσθ’ ἵσταμαι, οὐδὲ μεγαίρω (sc. διαπέρσαι) 4.54, cf. Call. Del. 163. c. dat. pers. only, feel a grudge towards, Δαναοῖσι μεγήρας Il. 15.473. abs., ἢ πὺξ ἠὲ πάλῃ ἢ καὶ ποσίν, οὔ τι μεγαίρω I care not which, Od. 8.206. c. gen. rei, ἀμενήνωσεν δέ οἱ αἰχμὴν… Ποσειδάων, βιότοιο μεγήρας Poseidon baffled his spear grudging him the life [of Antilochus, Il. 13.563 ; οὐ μ. τοῦδέ σοι δωρήματος A. Pr. 626 ; μοι… ἐμέγηρε τόκοιο ARh. 1.289. Pass., to be envied, AP 9.645.10 (Maced.). = βασκαίνειν, bewitch, ὄμμασι… ἐμέγηρεν ὀπωπάς ARh. 4.1670. (Said to be a Salaminian word, Sch. Il. 13.563 ; in late Prose, as etym. of Μέγαιρα, Corn. ND 10.)

ες, (cf. κητώεις) yawning, with mighty hollows, μεγακήτεα πόντον Od. 3.158 ; with mighty maw, δελφίς Il. 21.22 ; capacious, νηῦς 8.222, 11.5, 600. (Also expld. as derived from κῆτος, μ. πόντος teeming with monsters, μ. νηῦς with a monster as figurehead.)
pr. n., v. μεγακλεής.
ές, very famous, acc. (as if from μεγακλής) μεγακλέα Opp. C. 2.4.
ές, much renowned, IG 3.1335, 12(5).677 (Syros), Man. 2.150.
ον, unjust in great matters, opp. μικραδικητής, Arist. Rh. 1391a29.
ές, = μεγαλοσθενής, Hsch.
Adv. splendidly, munificently, προσφέρεσθαι πρὸς τὸν δῆμον Michel 731.4 (Ilium, ii BC). [To be deleted (Suppl.)]
ον, with spacious ways, Hsch. s.v. εὐρυόδεια.
μεγάλοι ἄνδρες, ἢ μεγάλοι κατὰ τὴν ἀνδρείαν, ἢ πολυανδροῦντες, Hsch.
Dor. for μεγαληνορία.
Dor. for μεγαλήνωρ.
(sc. ἱερά), τά, (< ἄρτος) feast of great loaves, kept by the Delians in honour of Demeter, Semus 13.
ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Halos, IG 9(2).109.
ον, epith. of Demeter in Boeotia, Polem.Hist. 39.

boast, brag, A. Ag. 1528 (anap.), LXX Ez. 16.50, Ph. 1.284, AP 5.272 (Agath.) ; ἐπί τινι Plb. 12.13.10 ; ἐν ταῖς εὐπραγίαις Id. 8.21.11 ; διά τι DS. 15.16 ; — also in Med., Pl. Alc. 1.104c, R. 395d ; ἐπί τινι App. BC 1.13. c. acc., boast of, μονομάχιον Id. Gall. 10.
ατος, τό, matter for boasting, τὸ μ. καὶ ἀξίωμα Ph. 2.434, cf. Sm. Ez. 32.12.
ενος, ὁ, ἡ, with large neck, Olymp. Hist. p. 459 D., Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. ἐριαύχενας, Hsch. s.v. ἐρισφάραγος.
ές, = μεγάλαυχος, Orph. H. 63.3, IG 14.433 (Tauromenium), Man. 3.34, Vett.Val. 272.8.
one must boast, Ph. 1.217.
ον, much vaunted, Epigr. ap. Paus. 1.13.3.

ἡ, I. boasting, arrogance, Pl. Tht. 174d (pl.), Ly. 206a, LXX 4 Ma. 2.15.
II. exultation, Longin. 7.2.
ον, boastful, vainglorious, Pi. P. 8.15, A. Pers. 533 (anap.), Pl. Ly. 206a (Comp.), Ph. 1.121 ; τὸ μ., = μεγαλαυχία 1, X. Ages. 8.1. Adv. Sup. -ότατα, εἰπεῖν Max.Tyr. 7.7.

α, ον, (< μέγας) magnificent, splendid, ῥήματα X. Mem. 2.1.34 (Comp.) ; κτῆμα ib. 4.5.2 ; μ. τι διαπεπραγμένος Men. Per. Fr. 1, cf. Phld. Rh. 2.6 S. ; πίστιν μεγαλειοτάταν prob. in Paean ap. Plu. Flam. 16 (Coll. Alex. p. 173 P.) ; τὸ μ. τῶν πράξεων, τῆς ἀθανασίας, Plb. 8.1.1, SIG 798.4 (i AD), cf. Vett.Val. 70.1 ; τὰ μ. mighty works, LXX De. 11.2, al., Act. Ap. 2.11. Adv. -ως greatly, ὠφελῶν τὴν πόλιν X. Ages. 11.16, Plb. 3.87.5 ; magnificently, μ. εἴρηκας Pl. Hp. Ma. 291e ; ὀψωνεῖν Antiph. 192 ; θεοὺς μ. τιμᾶν X. Oec. 11.9 ; Comp. -ότερον Pl. Tht. 168c ; -οτέρως, γαμεῖν X. HG 4.1.9. of persons, stately, haughty, Id. Mem. 4.1.4. τὸ μ. τινός, as a title, Highness, POxy. 1204.10 (iii AD), etc. of style, elevated, Demetr. Eloc. 14, al. Adv. Sup. -ότατα, ἑρμηνεῦσαι Philostr. VS 1.21.1.

ητος, ἡ, majesty, magnificence, LXX Je. 40 (33).9, Ev. Luc. 9.43, Ath. 4.130f, Dam. Pr. 94 ; ἡ τῶν πυραμίδων μ. OGI 666.26 (Egypt, i AD) ; of a person, greatness, Supp.Epigr. 3.583.6 (Olbia, ii/iii AD).
as a title, Majesty, ἡ σὴ μ. J. AJ 8.4.3, cf. CPHerm. 52.23 (iii AD) ; ἐν ταῖς μ. γενήσεται Vett.Val. 70.4 ; also, = Lat. majestas, ἡ μ. τοῦ Ῥωμαίων δήμου PGiss. 40i 11 (iii AD).
ή, όν, amplified, of compound words, prob. in Arist. Po. 1457a35.
ὁ, wholesale merchant, Sch. Ar. Av. 823.
ον, attempting great objects, Plb. 15.37.1, DS. 1.19 ; μεγαλεπήβολος is v.l., cf. Suid.
ον, harbouring great designs, Corn. ND 22.

talk big, boast, X. An. 6.3.18 ; with neut. Adj., ἕκαστα ἐμεγαληγόρουν Id. Cyr. 4.44.2, cf. 7.1.17 ; also τοιοῦτόν τινα λόγον μ. Polem. Cyn. 45.
trans., extol highly, Hdn. 3.9.12.

ἡ, big talking, E. Heracl. 356 (pl., lyr.), X. Ap. 1, Man. 2.468 (pl.).
elevation, sublimity of diction, DH. Th. 27, Demetr. Eloc. 29.

ον, talking big, vaunting, A. Th. 565 (lyr.), X. Cyr. 7.1.17. Adv. -ρως App. Hisp. 19, Mith. 70.
lofty, magniloquent, Longin. 8.4.

Dor. μεγαλανορία, ἡ, manliness, self-confidence, Pi. N. 11.44 (pl.).
haughtiness, E. Ph. 184 (lyr., sed -ηγορ- Sch.).

Dor. μεγαλάνωρ, ορος, ὁ, ἡ, (< ἀνήρ) high-souled, epith. of Ἡσυχία, Pi. Fr. 109.
haughty, Id. P. 1.52.

ορος, ὁ, ἡ, (< ἦτορ) greathearted, Πάτροκλος Il. 16.257 ; Κύκλωψ Od. 10.200, cf. DP. 658, etc. ; in Hom. always with pr. ns., exc. in phrase μεγαλήτορα θυμόν Il. 9.629, Od. 9.500, al. ; μεγαλήτορες ὀργαί Pi. I. 5 (4).34.
ον, in lofty strain, ὕμνος prob. for μελαν- in Orph. A. 421 (μέλανα σκότον Abel).
Pass., to be exalted, bear oneself proudly, μηδὲ μεγαλίζεο θυμῷ Il. 10.69 ; οὔτ’ ἄρ τι μεγαλίζομαι οὔτ’ ἀθερίζω Od. 23.174. — Ep. word.
η, ον, late Sup. of μέγας, μ. δίφθογγος Sch. D.T. p. 199 H.

μύρον, a perfumed unguent named after the inventor Megallos (cf. Ar. Fr. 536, Stratt. 33), Pherecr. 140, Anaxandr. 46, Eub. 90.6, Amphis 27, cf. Dsc. 1.58 ; — wrongly written μεγαλεῖον in Thphr. Od. 29, al.
ον, illustrious in life, Paul.Al. N. 2.
ές, greatly injuring, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. ἄη.
α, ὁ, loudshouting, κήρυκες Agath. 4.1.
ον, gloss on ἠερίβοια, Eust. 562.40.
ον, gloss on ἱππόβοτος, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s. h. v.
ον, high-counselling, Pap. in Sitzb. Heidelb. Akad. 1923 (2).14, Sch. rec. A. Pr. 18.
ου, ὁ, loud-thundering, Ζεύς QS. 2.508.
ον, loud-roaring, ὕδωρ Orph. A. 463.
ον, loud-bellowing, λέων QS. 5.188.
ον, with large clods, Sch. D Il. 1.155.
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, big-bellied, Sch. A. Th. 1035.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, hugeness, Democr. 3.
entertain noble sentiments, DC. 63.25.
ἡ, loftiness of sentiment, X. Ages. 8.3.
ον, gen. ονος, of lofty sentiments, high-minded, X. Oec. 21.8 ; τὸ μ., = μεγαλογνωμοσύνη, Philostr. Ep. 73, cf. X. Ages. 9.6.
write with ω μέγα, opp. μικρογραφέω, Sch. A. Pers. 297, Hdn. Epim. 193, 200, Jo. Sic. in Rh. 6.89 W., etc.
ἡ, painting on a large scale, Vitr. 7.4.4.
ον, munificent, διάθεσις IGRom. 4.1302.27 (Aeolis).
ον, full of large trees, Str. 3.2.3, 3.4.2.
ον, quite evident, manifest, Sch. B Il. 11.155.
ἡ, high opinion of oneself, in pl., Suid. s.v. ψολοκομπία.
ον, very glorious, Εὐνομία Pi. O. 9.16 ; κύριος OGI 90.1 (Rosetta, ii BC) ; Ῥώμη Plu. Thes. 1, cf. Herm. ap. Stob. 1.49.44. Adv. -ξως LXX 3 Ma. 6.39.
ὁ, great slave, opp. μικρόδουλος, Arr. Epict. 4.1.55.
οντος, ὁ, ἡ, with large teeth, gloss on ἀργιόδους, EM 137.6.
ἡ, great power, Hsch. s.v. ἐρισθενέος.
ον, very powerful, Herm. in Phdr. p. 176 A., PMagLond. 121.881, PMagLeid. V. 11.24.
make large presents, J. AJ 12.4.9.
ἡ, munificence, Luc. Sat. 4, DMort. 6.4, Anach. 9, Hld. 9.24, CPHerm. 121.13 (iii AD) ; pl., Hdn. 2.3.9.

ον, munificent, τύχη Democr. 176, cf. Max.Tyr. 17.2 ; μεγαλοδωρότατε δαιμόνων Ar. Pax 393 (lyr.), cf. Plb. 10.5.6, CPHerm. 119 viii 2 (iii AD) ; τὸ μ., = μεγαλοδωρία, Plu. Ant. 4, 43. Adv. -ρως Poll. 3.119, Jul. Or. 6.194d.
Adv. on a large scale, οἱ τὰ σώματα διηρθρωμένοι μ. Philostr. Gym. 36.
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, clad in a large robe, Eust. 1430.25.
contr. μεγαλουργέω, do great things, Ph. 2.142 ; — Pass., Id. 1.428, al.
ατος, τό, great achievement, Ph. 2.107, 174 (pl.).
contr. μεγαλουργής, ές, performing great deeds, Gloss. Adv. -γῶς ib.
ἡ, great achievement, Plb. 30.25.1 (s.v.l.) ; contr. μεγαλουργία, Str. 3.5.6, Ph. 2.143, J. AJ 2.7.1 ; magnificence, ib. 8.3.2, al., Luc. Cal. 17.
ή, όν, contr. μεγαλουργικός, Procl. in Alc. p. 137 C.
contr. μεγαλουργός, όν, = μεγαλοεργής ; τὸ μ., = μεγαλοεργία, Plu. Caes. 58, Luc. Alex. 4, Procl. in Prm. p. 663 S., al.
ον, very zealous, gloss on ἀγάζηλος, EM 5.29.
ον, gloss on λιπαρόζωνος, Sch. E. Ph. 175.
εως, ἡ, v.l. for μακροημέρευσις, LXX Si. 30.22.
ον, loud-sounding, gloss on ἐρικλάγκτας, Sch. Pi. P. 12.38 ; on ἐριβρεμέτης and ἐρίβρομος, Hsch.
τριχος, ὁ, ἡ, with strong or thick hair, Gloss.
ον, = μεγάθυμος, Pl. R. 375c, Thd. Pr. 19.19.
τό, great sacrifice, Sch. Lyc. 329 (ed. Bachm.).
ον, very wretched, Theoc. 2.72.
ές, with a large curve, Orib. 45.6.6.
ον, with large fruit, Thphr. HP 4.4.5.
ον, with large stalk, Thphr. HP 7.6.3.
ων, gen. ω, with large horns, Eust. 634.56, Sch. Oppian. H. 2.290.
ές, concealing much ; capacious, θάλαμοι Pi. P. 2.33.
ον, with large head, Arist. Somn. Vig. 457a23, Pr. 955b7, Gal. 19.454.
ον, braving great dangers, adventurous, opp. μικροκίνδυνος, Arist. EN 1124b8.
ές, glorious, B. 7.49, Lyr.Adesp. Oxy. 860 (a).10.
ῆτος, ὁ, ἡ, gloss on ἀνδροκμῆσι (i.e. Ἁδροκμῆσι), Sch. A. Eu. 248.
ον, with large ventricles, Arist. PA 667a29 ; with large intestinal canal, Mnesith. ap. Orib. 21.7.6, 7 (Sup.) ; — written μεγαλόκοιλος (= προγάστωρ) in Gal. 6.467.
v. μεγαλοκοίλιος.
ον, full-bosomed, Νύξ B. Fr. 23 (leg. μελανό-).
ον, (κόρη III) with large pupils, Aët. 7.54.
ον, with lofty summits, γῆ Lyc. Orator ap. Arist. Rh. 1405b36.
ον, gloss on ζάκοτος, Sch. Pi. Pae. 9.18, EM 407.16. Adv. -τως, gloss on ζαφελῶς, Hsch.
ον, loud-screaming, gloss on ἐρικλάγκτας, Sch. Pi. P. 12.38.
ές, far-ruling, Ῥώμη AP 9.657 (Marian.).
ορος, ὁ, = μεγαλοκρατής, LXX 3 Ma. 6.2.
ον, gloss on ἐρίγδουπος, Hsch.
ον, gen. ονος, making great waves, Arist. Pr. 942a14.
ον, large-limbed, of a locust, Dsc. 2.52.
ον, talking big or much, Gloss.
ον, (μᾶζα) = μεγάλαρτος, epith. of Demeter in Boeotia, Polem.Hist. 39.
ές, very frantic, Sch. S. Aj. 143.
ον, with large breasts, Gp. 19.2.4.

ἡ, largeness of parts, opp. μικρομέρεια, Arist. Metaph. 989a6, Thphr. Ign. 45. generally, largeness of scale, great size, μ. καὶ δύναμις Plb. 1.26.9 ; τόπου IG 9(2).1109.77 (Coropa).
lavishness, munificence, OGI 168.58 (Syene, ii BC), Sammelb. 4321.4 (ii BC).

ές, consisting of large particles, Pl. Ti. 62a (Comp.), Arist. Cael. 303b27. Adv. -ρῶς, κατάγνυται (of bone) Gal. 14.792.
magnificent, sumptuous, Plb. 28.20.1 ; παρασκευὴ καὶ πότος Id. 30.14.1 ; δεῖπνα IG 7.2712.61 (Acraeph.), cf. LXX 3 Ma. 5.8, etc. Adv. -ρῶς, χρῆσθαί τινι OGI 339.68 (Sestos, ii BC), cf. Plb. 16.25.3, 31.28.6, LXX 3 Ma. 6.33, Phld. Piet. p. 93 G., Ant.Lib. 18.1, etc. ; Comp. -έστερον Plb. 24.5.5.
ον, gloss on εὐρυμέτωπος, EM 396.50.
ἡ τῆς μητρὸς μήτηρ, Hsch.
τι, of high design, ambitious, A. Ag. 1426 (lyr.).
ον, great and small at once ; τὸ μ. Ph. 2.61.
ον, receiving high pay, Luc. Apol. 15, Herm. 57, Ath. 13.569a.
ἡ, magnificence, Aristeas 21 (dub.).
οῦ, ὁ, loud bellower, gloss on μεγάμυκος, Hsch.

ἡ, magnanimity, Pl. Lg. 935b, J. BJ 1.21.12, Plu. 2.401d, Luc. Apol. 9, Ael. NA 15.22.
elevation of thought, Luc. Pisc. 22, Simp. in Ph. 1147.5. as honorific title, ἡ ὑμετέρα μ. PFlor. 303.7 (vi AD).

ον, contr. μεγαλόνους, ουν, great-minded, magnanimous, Adam. 1.11, al. ; τὸ φύσει μ. J. BJ 1.21.5, cf. 5.5.8, Luc. Im. 18 ; metapl. pl. -νοες Polem. Phgn. 29.
elevated in diction, ὕμνοι Men. Rh. p. 336 S. (Comp. -ούστερος).
ουν, contr. for μεγαλόνοος.
ἡ, patience, fortitude, Plu. 2.551c (s.v.l.).
ον, with great cheeks, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. ἱππόβοτος.
ές, gloss on νηπενθές, EM 604.34.
ον, on the mighty rock, Ἀκρόπολις Ar. Lys. 482 (lyr.).
ον, = μεγαλόπλουτος, Sch. E. Hec. 493.
ον, exceeding rich, Eub. 37, DS. 15.58.
ον, contr. μεγαλόπνους, ουν, breathing strongly, Apollon.Soph. Lex. s.v. ζαής.
ουν, contr. for μεγαλόπνοος.

do great things, LXX Si. 50.22.
trans., magnify, τὰ ἴδια Hierocl. ap. Stob. 4.27.20.
ον, great in war, J. AJ 12.11.2.

epith. of great cities, αἱ μεγαλοπόλιες Ἀθᾶναι Pi. P. 7.1 ; μεγαλοπόλιες ὦ Συράκοσαι ib. 2.1 ; ἁ μ. Τροία E. Tr. 1291 (lyr.) ; Ἀθθίς Pae.Delph. 8 ; ἡ λαμπροτάτη μ. Ἀλεξάνδρεια PLips. 45.13 (iv AD) ; also of the κόσμος, Ph. 1.4, al.
ου, ὁ, citizen of a large city, Ph. 1.34, Poll. 9.25.
ον, wicked in great things, Arist. Pol. 1295b9.
ὁ, gloss on ἱππόπορνος, Phot.
ὁ, ἡ, πουν, τό, gen. ποδος, with large feet, Arist. HA 617a26.
ἡ, great fortune, App. BC 5.52.
ἡ, disposition to do great things, magnificence, Plu. Alc. 6, etc.
ον, gen. ονος, disposed to do great deeds, forming great designs, X. HG 5.2.36, Plu. Ages. 32.

Ion. μεγαλοπρεπείη, ἡ, magnificence, as a quality of persons, Hdt. 1.139, 3.125, Pl. R. 486a, Isoc. 9.2, Arist. EN 1107b17, etc. of style, elevation, DH. Comp. 16, Th. 23, Demetr. Eloc. 37. as a title, ἡ σὴ μ. Just. Nov. 41 Praef. ; ἡ αὐτοῦ μ. POxy. 1163.4 (v AD).

ές, befitting a great man, magnificent, δεῖπνον μ. Hdt. 5.18 ; δωρεὴν μεγαλοπρεπεστάτην Id. 6.122 ; κάλλιστον ἔργον καὶ μεγαλοπρεπέστατον Ar. Av. 1125 ; ταφή Pl. Mx. 234c ; προαίρεσις Hyp. Epit. 40 ; πράξεις ib. 1 (Comp.) ; δόξα 2 Ep. Pet. 1.17, etc. of persons, Pl. R. 487a, al., Arist. EN 1107b17 ; τὸ μ. X. Mem. 3.10.5 ; of a horse, Id. Eq. 10.1 (Comp.) ; Sup., as honorific title, PGrenf. 2.81 (a).14 (v AD), etc. of style, μ. λόγοι Pl. Smp. 210d ; λέξις Arist. Rh. Al. 1441b12 ; μεθιστάναι ἐπὶ τὸ μεγαλοπρεπέστερον ib. 1423b12. Adv. -πέως, Att. -πῶς, Hdt. 6.128, X. An. 1.4.17, etc. ; Comp. -έστερον Id. Vect. 6.1, Pl. Ly. 215e ; Sup. -έστατα Hdt. 7.57.
ον, with great wings, LXX Ez. 17.3, 7.
ὁ, magnificently poor, Διογένης τοὺς μεγάλα καὶ ἀθρόα λαμβάνοντας μεγαλοπτώχους ἐκάλει Stob. 3.10.62.
ον, gloss on εὐρυπυλής (-εύς cod.), Hsch.
ον, (< ῥίς) with large nose, Suid. s.v. λαρινοὶ βόες.
ου, ὁ, one who does great things, Adam. 2.39.
to be a boaster, LXX Ju. 6.17, Str. 13.1.40.
ἡ, big talking, Sch. S. Ant. 1350 (pl.).
ἡ, = μεγαλορρημονία, LXX 1Ki. 2.3, Philostr. Her. 2.19, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. σεμνομυθοῦσιν.
ον, gen. ονος, talking big, LXX Ps. 11 (12).4, Men. Prot. p. 11 D. ; in good sense, magniloquent, Philostr. VA 6.11. Adv. -όνως Poll. 9.147.
ον, with large roots, Dsc. 2.156, dub.l. in Thphr. CP 2.3.8 (ἐλαιηρότεραι cj. Wimmer).
ρρῶγος, ὁ, ἡ, with large berries, βότρυς Str. 15.2.14.
v. μέγας.
ον, great of flesh, LXX Ez. 16.26.
ές, of great strength, Hom. Epigr. 6, Pi. P. 6.21, Corinna 2, LXX 3 Ma. 5.13 ; epith. of Horus, Herm. ap. Stob. 1.49.44 ; of Heracles, IG 5(1).1119 (Geronthrae).
ον, gloss on δάσκιος, EM 248.51.
ον, loud-resounding, Luc. JTr. 1.
οῦ, ὁ, = μέγας σοφιστής, Ath. 3.113d.

ον, with enlarged abdomen, Hp. Acut. 53 ; with large viscera, Mnesith. ap. Orib. 21.7.6 (Sup.).
causing the viscera to swell, οἶνος μ. σπληνὸς καὶ ἥπατος Hp. Acut. 50.
high-spirited, ψυχή E. Med. 109 (anap.).
ον, gloss on ἐριστάφυλος, Sch. D Od. 9.358.
υ, with large spikes, νάρδος Dsc. 1.7, cf. Thphr. HP 8.4.3.
ον, gloss on ἀγάστονος, EM 8.54.
ον, broad-chested, Philostr. Gym. 39.
ον, = μεγαλόστερνος, Mnesith. ap. Orib. 21.7.6 (Sup.).
ον, with large mouth, Arist. PA 662a25.
ον, most piteous, πήματα A. Pr. 413 (lyr.).
ον, with a large pulse, Gal. 2.387, 412, 8.710.
ον, bulky, of particles, Thphr. CP 6.1.6.
ον, gen. ονος, magnificent, A. Pr. 408 (lyr.).
ον, large-bodied, Eust. 962.23, Sch. Oppian. H. 1.360.
ον, = μεγαλοσώματος, Sch. Ar. Ra. 55, etc.
ὁ, engineer, Arist. Mu. 398b14 (s.v.l.) ; τὸ μ., = ὕψος, the sublime, DH. Isoc. 3.
ητος, ἡ, = μέγεθος, Chrysipp. Stoic. 3.60.
ον, greatly honoured, PMagLeid. W. 14.22, Pap. in Sitzb. Heidelb. Akad. 1923 (2).18 ; gloss on ἐρίτιμος, Hsch., EM 374.55. Adv. -μως DL. 8.88.
ον, greatly adventurous, J. AJ 5.1.29, App. Syr. 10 (Comp.), Luc. Alex. 8.
ον, with large bow, gloss on ἄβιοι, EM 3.23.
ον, large-necked, gloss on ἐριαύχην, EM 142.12.
contr. for μεγαλοεργέω.
contr. for μεγαλοεργής.
contr. for μεγαλοεργία.
contr. for μεγαλοεργικός.
contr. for μεγαλοεργός.
μεγαλαυχία, ὑψηλοφροσύνη, Hsch.
ον, lordly, overweening, βία B. 16.23 (nisi leg. -αυχον).
ές, = μεγαλοπρεπής 2, ὄνος Arist. (?) in PLit. Lond. 112 (Sup.), cf. Paul.Al. N. 2, Hsch., Phot.
ές, gloss on βυσσοφαρής, Hsch.
ές, gloss on ζαφλεγέες, Hsch.
ον, large-eyed, Arist. Phgn. 811b20, PPetr. 3 p. 31 (iii BC), Plu. 2.299b, Ptol. Tetr. 143, Olymp. Hist. p. 459 D.
ον, having great friends, Paul.Al. N. 2, Cat.Cod.Astr. 8(4).136.
ον, large-veined, Arist. PA 667a30.

to be high-minded, μ. ἐφ’ ἑαυτῷ to be confident in oneself, X. HG 6.2.39 ; πρὸς τὰς ἀνάγκας LXX 4 Ma. 6.24 ; to be generous, DC. 43.21, al. ; — Med., display high spirit, περὶ τῆς ἡγεμονίας J. AJ 19.3.1. in bad sense, to be arrogant, Plu. Dio 40, al. ; — in Med., Pl. R. 528c ; ἐπί τινι DC. 43.14 ; τινι Philostr. VA 8.5 ; πρός τινα… ὡς… ib. 1.39.

ἡ, greatness of mind, Pl. Smp. 194b, Isoc. 9.27, IG 7.2713.10 (Oratio Neronis), Philostr. VS 2.1.3 ; ὑπὸ μεγαλοφροσύνης magnanimously, Hdt. 7.136. in bad sense, pride, arrogance, ib. 24 ; μ. γένους pride of family, Antipho 4.3.2 ; pl., proud thoughts, AP 5.298 (Agath.).
elevation of thought, Longin. 7.3, Demetr. Eloc. 298 ; ὕψος φροσύνης ἀπήχημα Longin. 9.2.

ονος, ὁ, ἡ, (< φρήν) high-minded, generous, Protag. 9 ; Ἡσυχία Ar. Lys. 1289 codd. (lyr.), cf. Isoc. 2.25 ; Comp., Id. 12.60, 242, Luc. Am. 52 ; μ. εἰς δαπάνην Gal. 13.954 ; τὸ μ. X. Ages. 11.11. Adv. -όνως J. AJ 6.6.5, OGI 566.12 (Oenoanda) ; Sup. -έστατα, εἰπεῖν Philostr. VS 2.1.3. in bad sense, arrogant ; in Adv. -όνως Pl. Euthd. 293a, X. HG 4.5.6.

ές, (< φυή) of noble nature, ἄνδρα μεγαλοφυέστερον ἢ κατ’ ἄνθρωπον Plb. 12.23.5, cf. Dam. Pr. 54 (Comp.) ; οἱ μ. τῶν ἀνθρώπων S.E. P. 1.12, cf. Arr. Epict. 3.23.15 ; μ. ἤθη καὶ πάθη DH. Vett. Cens. 2.11 ; ἡ μ. αὐθεντία σου, as a title, Just. Nov. 126.3 Ep. Adv. -φυῶς Arr. Epict. 2.17.19.
endowed with genius, Phld. Rh. 1.28 S., DL. 1.38 ; τὸ μ. lofty genius, Longin. 9.1 ; τὸ μεγαλοφυέστατον Id. 34.4.
large, ἀμφίβια (in the Nile), Str. 15.1.22. Adv. -φυῶς in bad sense, with exaggeration, Cleom. 2.1.

ἡ, nobleness of nature, Iamb. VP 23.103 (pl.), Phlp. in de An. 529.14, Hsch.
genius, talent, Longin. 13.2, 36.4, Apollod. Poliorc. 138.16.
ον, large-leaved, Thphr. CP 2.10.2 ; Comp., Id. HP 7.4.4.
part. -φωνῶν f.l. in Phot. s.v. ἱεροφωνῶν (leg. -φώνων).

ἡ, loudness of voice, Arist. GA 787a3, DS. 16.92.
grandiloquence, Luc. Hist. Conscr. 8, JTr. 6, Philostr. VS 1.21.5, Men. Rh. p. 369 S.

ον, loudvoiced, Hp. Epid. 6.4.19 (Sup.), Arist. GA 787a12, Pr. 899a9 ; Comp. -ότερος Luc. Bis Acc. 11 ; Sup. -ότατος DS. 11.34. Adv. -νως Poll. 2.113, Suid. s.v. τορόν. loud-talker, bawler, D. 19.238.
grandiloquent, Philostr. VS 2.10.1 ; ποιητής Id. Ep. 16 ; ὁ μεγαλοφωνότατος, of Pindar, Ath. 13.564d ; of Homer, Luc. Musc. Enc. 5.
ον, greatly rejoiced over, gloss on μεγήριτος, Hsch.
ον, gen. ονος, wide-gaping, χάνναι Epich. 67.
ον, gloss on ἀγάστονος, EM 8.54.
ον, loud-sounding, Hsch. s.v. ἐρίγδουπος, Sch. Ar. Nu. 284.
to be generous, Hsch. s.v. δαψιλέστατος.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, greatness of soul, highmindedness, lordliness, Democr. 46, Isoc. 9.59, Arist. EN 1107b22, 1123a34, Plb. 10.40.6, etc. ; μ. τῶν ἔργων D. 23.205, cf. DS. 1.58 ; generosity, πρός τινας IG2². 1326.25 ; pl., Plb. 1.64.5. in bad sense, arrogance, D. 18.68, v.l. in Luc. Tim. 28.
Quixotism, Pl. Alc. 2.150c.

ον, high-souled, generous, Isoc. 9.3, Arist. EN 1123b2 ; εὐεργετικὸς καὶ μ. Plb. 22.21.3 ; τὸ μ., = μεγαλοψυχία, Id. 1.20.11, 31.28.9, Plu. Per. 36 ; Comp. -ότερος, φαίνεσθαι D. 19.235, cf. Hyp. Eux. 33. Adv. -χως, ἔχειν πρός τινας D. 19.140 ; χρήσασθαι τοῖς πράγμασι Plb. 1.8.4, cf. OGI 194.11 (Egypt, i BC) ; ἐνεγκεῖν συμφοράν Plu. CG 19.
romantic, Quixotic, Pl. Alc. 2.140c.

fut. μεγαλυνῶ LXX Ge. 12.2, al. ; aor. ἐμεγάλυνα ib. Ec. 2.4, al. ; — Pass., fut. -υνθήσομαι ib. Za. 12.11, al. ; aor. -ύνθην ib. Ma. 1.5, al. ; pf. part. μεμεγαλυμμένος Aq. Ps. 143 (144).12 ; (< μέγας) : — make great or powerful, exalt, τοὺς πολεμίους Th. 5.98 ; — Pass., μεγαλύνεσθαι ἐκ τῶν συμβαινόντων gain great glory by…, X. HG 7.1.24, cf. Ep. Phil. 1.20, POxy. 1592.3 (iii/iv AD).
make great by word, extol, magnify, τὸ ὄνομά τινος E. Ba. 320 ; μ. τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δύναμιν παρά τινι Th. 8.81 ; ἑαυτόν X. Ap. 32 ; μ. τὴν Λακεδαίμονα πρὸς Ἀθηναίους Plu. Cim. 16 ; τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν δύναμιν DS. 1.20 ; freq. in LXX, ll. cc. ; — Med., boast oneself, περί τινος Sappho 35 ; γέννα in point of birth, A. Pr. 892 (lyr.) ; οὐδὲ μεγαλύνεται ἐπὶ τῷ ἔργῳ X. Hier. 2.17, cf. Oec. 21.4 ; ταῦτ’ ἀκούων ἐμεγαλύνετο Id. Mem. 3.6.3.
magnify, exaggerate, Th. 6.28, Phld. Rh. 1.173 S., Ir. p. 45 W., DC. Fr. 57.81, al.
ον, gloss on ἐριώδυνος, Hsch.
ατος, τό, might, ῥάβδος μεγαλώματος LXX Je. 31 (48).17.

ον, with a great name, giving glory, νίκα S. Ant. 148 (lyr.) ; Ζεῦ Ar. Th. 315 (lyr.), cf. Nu. 569 (lyr.) ; κύριος LXX Je. 39 (32).19.
Math. in Comp., having a higher denominator, Iamb. in Nic. p. 50 P., al. Adv. -ωτέρως ib. p. 85 P.
όν, large-eyed, Opp. C. 2.177.
Adv. of μέγας.

Adv. of μέγας, far and wide, over a vast space, κεῖτο μέγας μ. Il. 16.776, cf. 18.26 ; κεῖσο μέγας μ. Od. 24.40, cf. Sappho Supp. 20a. 18. v.l. for μεγάλως, Hdt. 2.161, Arr. An. 4.12.1, al. = μεγαλοπρεπῶς, Hdt. 5.67, 6.70, Plb. 28.13.5, Luc. Zeux. 8. — Ep., Ion., and late Prose.
ἡ, greatness, majesty, LXX 2Ki. 7.21, al., Aristeas 192.
ές, (< ὄφελος) very serviceable, Phld. Mus. p. 104 K., Corn. ND 16, Plu. 2.553c, Cleom. 1.1 (Sup.), Sor. 2.14.
ον, loud-braying, ὄνος Hsch.
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, = μεγαλήνωρ, πλοῦτος Pi. O. 1.2.
τά, Megara, Hdt. 5.76, etc. ; Μέγαράδε to Megara, Ar. Ach. 524.
έως, ὁ, citizen of Megara, Thgn. 23, etc. ; pl. Μεγαρέες, εῖς, -ῆς, Hdt. 1.59, etc. ; prov., Μεγαρέων δάκρυα ΄crocodile΄s tears΄ (because of the quantity of onions grown near Megara), Zen. 5.8.
side with the Megarians or speak their dialect, κλάων Μεγαριεῖς Ar. Ach. 822, cf. Sch. ad loc. follow the Megarian philosopher Stilpo, DL. 2.113.

ή, όν, Megarian, Ar. Ach. 522, etc. ; Μεγαρικοὶ κέραμοι, and in the language of trade Μεγαρικά, Megarian pottery, Sch. Ar. Nu. 1205 ; cf. Μαγαρικός ; Μεγαρικοί, οἱ, philosophers of the Megarian school, Arist. Metaph. 1046b29, DL. 2.106 ; οἱ M. διαλεκτικοί Phld. Rh. 1.279 S. ; M. ἐρωτήματα Chrysipp. Stoic. 2.90 ; fem. Μεγαρίς (sc. γῆ), Megarian territory, Th. 2.31, etc.
Adv. in the Megarian dialect, Hdn. Gr. 1.506.
Adv. from Megara, Sus. 1, Ar. V. 57.
Adv. at Megara, Ar. Ach. 758, IG1². 929.3.

pl. τὰ μέγαρα, pits sacred to Demeter and Persephone, into which young pigs were let down in the Thesmophoria, Paus. 9.8.1, Porph. Antr. 6, Sch. Luc. DMeretr. 1 ; — also written μάγαρον, Men. 1031. (cf. Hebr. mĕ`ārāh ΄cave΄.)
Adv. to the hall, to the women΄s room, Od. 16.413, al.

τό, gen. pl. μεγαρέων Sophr. 6 ; large room, hall ; esp. the chief room in the Homeric palace, μ. πλεῖον δαιτυμόνων Od. 17.604, al.
women΄s apartment, 18.198 ; pl., 17.569, 19.30.
bedchamber, 11.374. in pl., house, palace, freq. in Hom., ἐνὶ (ἐν) μεγάροισι Il. 1.396, 418, al. ; opp. ἐπ’ ἀγροῦ, Od. 22.47 ; later in sg., Pi. O. 6.2, P. 4.134.
sanctuary, shrine, freq. in Hdt. (whouses the word in thissense only), 1.47, 65, 2.143, 6.134.
tomb, Epigr.Gr. 453.2 (Batanaea).
εως, ἡ, (< μεγαίρω) jealousy, envy, Hsch.
ή, όν, envious, Hsch.

μεγάλη [α], μέγα, gen. μεγάλου, ης, ου, dat. μεγάλῳ, ῃ, ῳ, acc. μέγαν, μεγάλην, μέγα ; dual μεγάλω, α, ω ; pl. μεγάλοι, μεγάλαι, μεγάλα, etc. ; the stem μεγάλο- is never used in sg. nom. and acc. masc. and neut., and only once in voc. masc., ὦ μεγάλε Ζεῦ A. Th. 822 (anap.).
big, of bodily size ; freq. of stature, εἶδος… μ. ἦν ὁράασθαι Od. 18.4 ; κεῖτο μ. μεγαλωστί Il. 16.776 ; ἠΰς τε μ. τε Od. 9.508 ; φῶτα μέγαν καὶ καλόν ib. 513 ; καλή τε μεγάλη τε 15.418 ; κάρτα μεγάλη καὶ εὐειδής Hdt. 3.1 ; φύσιν τίν’ εἶχε φράζε ; Answ. μέγας S. OT 742.
full-grown, of age as shown by stature, νῦν δ’ ὅτε δὴ μ. εἰμί Od. 2.314 ; μήτε μέγαν μήτ’ οὖν νεαρῶν τινα A. Ag. 358 (anap.) ; later, elder of two persons of the same name, Wilcken Chr. 305 (iii BC) ; Σκιπίων ὁ μ. Plb. 18.35.9. of animals, μ. ἵπποι, βοῦς, σῦς, Il. 2.839, 18.559, Od. 19.439 ; αἰετός Pi. I. 6 (5).50. generally, vast, high, οὐρανός, ὄρος, πύργος, Il. 1.497, 16.297, 6.386 ; wide, πέλαγος, λαῖτμα θαλάσσης, Od. 3.179, 5.174 ; long, ἠϊών, αἰγιαλός, Il. 12.31, 2.210 ; sts. opp. ὀλίγος, κῦμα οὔτε μέγ’ οὔτ’ ὀ. Od. 10.94 ; but usu. opp. μικρός or σμικρός, πρὸς ἑαυτὸ ἕκαστον καὶ μ. καὶ σμικρόν Anaxag. 3 ; τὸ ἄπειρον ἐκ μεγάλου καὶ μικροῦ Arist. Metaph. 987b26, etc. of quality or degree, great, mighty, freq. epith. of gods, ὁ μ. Ζεύς A. Supp. 1052 (lyr.), etc. ; μεγάλα θεά, of Demeter and Persephone, S. OC 683 (lyr.) ; θεοὶ μεγάλοι, of the Cabiri, IG 12(8).71 (Imbros), etc. ; Μήτηρ μ., of Cybele, SIG 1014.83 (Erythrae, iii BC), 1138.3 (Delos, ii BC) ; Μήτηρ θεῶν μ. OGI 540.6 (Pessinus), etc. ; Ἴσιδος μ. μητρὸς θεῶν PStrassb. 81.14 (ii BC) ; μ. ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων Act. Ap. 19.28 ; τίς θεὸς μ. ὡς ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν ; LXX Ps. 76 (77).13 ; ὁ μ. θεός Ep. Tit. 2.13 ; of men, μ. ἠδὲ κραταιός Od. 18.382 ; ὀλίγος καὶ μ.
